title: Treasury Sanctions Major Drug Trafficking Organizations Supporting Terrorist Cartels
body: November 19, 2026 Coordinated Action with International Partners Targets a Cartel-Linked Outlaw Motorcycle Gang and Canadian-Based Mafia Leaders and Facilitators WASHINGTON —Today, the Department of the Treasury’s Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) sanctioned two international drug trafficking organizations: the Australia-headquartered Comanchero Outlaw Motorcycle Gang ( Comancheros ) and the Italy-based ‘Ndrangheta , a mafia-type criminal syndicate.  By providing essential logistical and operational support, the Comancheros and ‘Ndrangheta help terrorist cartels expand their international reach and sustain global narcotrafficking networks. “Cartels do not operate in isolation. They rely on other criminal organizations like the Comancheros and ‘Ndrangheta to move drugs, launder illicit proceeds, and ultimately poison Americans with narcotics,” said Secretary of the Treasury Scott Bessent .  “Treasury will continue to expose and disrupt narcoterrorism networks to Keep America Safe.” The Comancheros and the ‘Ndrangheta operate sophisticated transnational criminal networks that facilitate large-scale drug trafficking and money laundering. The ‘Ndrangheta controls a significant share of the European cocaine trade, while the Comancheros have helped open access to some of the world's most lucrative illicit drug markets. In keeping with President Trump’s pledge to eliminate cartels, OFAC has prioritized targeting these and other criminal groups that threaten the welfare of Americans. Treasury has coordinated closely with the Homeland Security Task Force (HSTF), taking nearly 40 actions against over 500 individuals and entities since the beginning of 2025.  OFAC uses a network-based approach to simultaneously disrupt as many different facets of the cartels as possible, from their leadership and key organizational nodes to facilitators and enablers, such as corrupt officials, complicit family members, and ostensibly legitimate front persons. Today’s action reflects a unified, whole-of-government effort to ensure operational coordination and maximize impact against transnational criminal networks.  OFAC conducted its investigation in parallel with the HSTF, with support from the Federal Bureau of Investigation, Drug Enforcement Administration, and Homeland Security Investigations.  OFAC continues to work closely with the HSTF to disrupt the flow of illicit drugs and dismantle the networks, facilitators, and financial infrastructure that enable their production and distribution. Additionally, OFAC worked closely with valued international partners, including the Australian Federal Police, New Zealand Police, Italy’s Guardia di Finanza, and Canada’s Royal Canadian Mounted Police and York Regional Police, whose cooperation was instrumental in supporting today’s action. The action was taken pursuant to Executive Order (E.O.) 14059, which targets the proliferation of illicit drugs and their means of production. COMANCHERO OUTLAW MOTORCYCLE GANG Today, OFAC designated the Comancheros , also known as the Comanchero Motorcycle Club or simply Comanchero MC , an Australian drug trafficking organization with an international footprint in Asia, Europe, and North America.  Developing strategic partnerships with U.S. sanctioned cartels, including the Sinaloa Cartel, CJNG, Clan del Golfo, and Los Choneros, the Comancheros have facilitated multi-hundred-kilogram shipments of cocaine from South America to the United States, Australia, and Europe.  The Comancheros have also been involved in other criminal activity around the world, including assassinations, arms trafficking, and money laundering. Because Australia and New Zealand are some of the world’s most lucrative illicit drug markets, Mexican cartels are increasingly targeting these markets to capitalize on the significantly higher margins and growing demand.  Due to the geographic distance from the major cocaine producing regions in the Western Hemisphere, cartels can charge substantial premiums compared to drugs sold in the United States.  The Sinaloa Cartel has been known to send “sleeper cells” to Australia to facilitate local drug distribution and establish contacts with the Comancheros and other outlaw motorcycle gangs who assist with the logistics of drug trafficking. The Comancheros are being designated under E.O. 14059 for having engaged in, or having attempted to engage in, activities or transactions that have materially contributed to, or pose a significant risk of materially contributing to, the international proliferation of illicit drugs or their means of production. COMANCHERO COMMAND AND CONTROL Alexandre Varela Villar , better known as Alex Vare ( Vare ), is the Spain-based World Commander of the Comancheros. Allan John Norman Meehan , better known as Allan Meehan ( Meehan ), is the Australia-based World President of the Comancheros. Pasilika Naufahu ( Pasilika ) is the national president of the New Zealand chapter of the Comancheros.  Before being deported to New Zealand in 2016, Pasilika was the sergeant-at-arms of the Comancheros in Australia.  Pasilika was arrested and sentenced to 10 years in prison in February 2021 for various charges related to his position in the Comancheros.  In close coordination with his brother and senior Comancheros member, Vetekina Naufahu ( Vetekina ), Pasilika has facilitated multi-hundred-kilogram importations of drugs into New Zealand and has established connections to the Sinaloa Cartel. Marco Francis Coffen ( Coffen ) is an associate of the Comancheros and has been involved in supplying multiple Australian criminal organizations, including the Comancheros, with encrypted communication platforms to drug traffickers and shielding them from police phone taps. Vare and Meehan are being designated pursuant to E.O. 14059 for being or having been leaders or officials of the Comancheros. Pasilika and Vetekina are being designated pursuant to E.O. 14059 for having acted or purported to act for or on behalf of, directly or indirectly, the Comancheros. Coffen is being designated pursuant to E.O. 14059 for having provided, or attempted to provide, financial, material, or technological support for, or goods or services in support of, the Comancheros. OMERTÀ – THE ‘NDRANGHETA The ‘Ndrangheta , an international drug trafficking organization and mafia-type criminal syndicate, operates in over 80 countries and continues to grow.  The ‘Ndrangheta’s adherence to omertà , a code of silence, and its reliance on deeply rooted familial bloodlines have enabled the organization to maintain secrecy, foster loyalty, resist infiltration, and expand its criminal influence across generations and international borders.  While the ‘Ndrangheta was founded in Calabria, Italy, the organization has expanded across Europe, the Western Hemisphere, and Australia.  As one of the largest criminal organizations in the world, the ‘Ndrangheta’s primary business comes from drug trafficking, with some estimates stating that almost 80 percent of the European cocaine trade is controlled by the ‘Ndrangheta.  While primarily focused on the cocaine trade, Italian officials have stated that the ‘Ndrangheta have started expanding into the illicit fentanyl market. The ’Ndrangheta frequently partner with Mexican and South American drug trafficking organizations and FTOs, including the Sinaloa Cartel, CJNG, and Clan del Golfo.  In the past, the ‘Ndrangheta has also partnered with other Mexican drug trafficking organizations and FTOs, including Los Zetas (now known as Cartel del Noreste) and the Gulf Cartel. The ‘Ndrangheta was previously designated on May 30, 2008 , pursuant to the Foreign Narcotics Kingpin Designation Act (Kingpin Act).  Today, the ‘Ndrangheta is being designated pursuant to E.O. 14059 for having engaged in, or having attempted to engage in, activities or transactions that have materially contributed to, or pose a significant risk of materially contributing to, the international proliferation of illicit drugs or their means of production. ‘NDRANGHETISTI NORTH OF THE BORDER Locali (singular: locale ) are the primary territorial organizational unit of the ‘Ndrangheta, comprising members known as ‘ ndranghetisti , that oversee and coordinate criminal activities within a specific geographical region.  The ‘Ndrangheta locale that operates in the Greater Toronto Area in Canada has strengthened in recent years, becoming so powerful that they dictate events in Italy from across the ocean.  In Canada, the ‘Ndrangheta is involved in drug trafficking, money laundering, murder, and other crimes.  This faction of the ‘Ndrangheta uses the U.S. and Canadian financial systems to launder illicit proceeds. Today, OFAC designated Italian-born Angelo Figliomeni (also known as “Don Angelino”), the leader of the Toronto faction of the ‘Ndrangheta.  A member of the Figliomeni ‘ndrina (family), Angelo Figliomeni fled to Canada in the early 2000’s to escape a 20-year sentence for weapons charges in Italy.  Angelo’s power extends beyond Canada, stretching back to Italy.  He has engaged in money laundering and other criminal activities on behalf of the ‘Ndrangheta. Another member of the Figliomeni ‘ndrina is Italian-born Cosimo Figliomeni (sometimes known as “Cosimino”), who is a top leader of the ‘Ndrangheta faction in Toronto and has been the subject of criminal proceedings in Italy in connection to his role within the ‘Ndrangheta organization. OFAC also designated two members of the Commisso ‘ndrina who are long time Italian-born leaders of the ‘Ndrangheta in Toronto. Francesco Commisso , also known as “U Scelto,” has faced allegations in Italy of being part of a Toronto oversight body that was tasked, among other duties, with imposing disciplinary sanctions on members. Rocco Remo Commisso (also known as Remo Commisso ) is a Canada-based leader of the ‘Ndrangheta and leads narcotics trafficking networks within the United States, including in the state of New York.  Remo Commisso was convicted in Canada in 1981 for conspiracy to commit murder and again in 1984 for his involvement in a bombing that killed one person.  Remo Commisso is involved in narcotics trafficking in the United States for the ‘Ndrangheta, including in New York. Vincenzo DeMaria (also known as Jimmy DeMaria ) is one of Toronto’s top ‘Ndrangheta bosses and has been active in the Toronto organized crime scene for decades.  DeMaria shot and killed a man in 1981 over a $2,000 drug debt and was convicted of second-degree murder in 1982.  He has since been released from prison and holds significant power in the ‘Ndrangheta. Cosimo Figliomeni, Francesco Commisso, Remo Commisso, and Jimmy DeMaria make up the Camera di Controllo of Toronto, a collegial body of the ‘Ndrangheta that decides on important questions concerning the organization and settles disputes, even outside of Toronto.  The Toronto ‘Ndrangheta is tightly connected throughout the world and has close relationships with members back in Calabria. Luigi Vescio Sr. (also known as “The Undertaker” or “Lui Vescio”) is a Canadian-born ‘Ndrangheta senior member and associate of Angelo Figliomeni and Jimmy DeMaria. Angelo Figliomeni, Cosimo Figliomeni, Francesco Commisso, Remo Commisso, and Luigi Vescio Sr. were all charged in the Italian Court of Reggio Calabria for mafia-type association related to their leadership, membership, and promotion of the ‘Ndrangheta in 2019. Angelo Figliomeni, Cosimo Figliomeni, Francesco Commisso, Remo Commisso, Jimmy DeMaria, and Luigi Vescio Sr. are being designated pursuant to E.O. 14059 for having acted or purported to act for or on behalf of, directly or indirectly, ‘Ndrangheta. FAMILY-OWNED, MAFIA-CONNECTED – VESCIO FUNERAL HOMES OFAC is also designating the corporate network of Vescio Sr., including his network of funeral homes in Ontario.  These funeral homes include the Fratelli Vescio Funeral Homes Ltd. in Woodbridge, Ontario, Vescio Funeral Homes Ltd. in Toronto and Vescio Funeral Home (Maple) Inc. in Maple, Ontario.  Vescio Sr. also controls a Toronto-based luxury limousine rental business, Phantom Limousine Services Inc. Vescio Sr. serves as the president of each of these companies. OFAC is also designating Luigi Vescio Sr.’s wife, Rose Vescio , and his two children, Luigi Vescio Jr. and Laura Vescio , for their roles in owning and operating the Vescio Funeral Homes on behalf of Luigi Vescio Sr. Rose Vescio, Luigi Vescio Jr., and Laura Vescio are being designated pursuant to E.O. 14059 for having acted or purported to act for or on behalf of, directly or indirectly, Luigi Vescio Sr. SANCTIONS IMPLICATIONS As a result of today’s action, all property and interests in property of the designated or blocked persons described above that are in the United States or in the possession or control of U.S. persons are blocked and must be reported to OFAC.  In addition, any entities that are owned, directly or indirectly, individually or in the aggregate, 50 percent or more by one or more blocked persons are also blocked.  Unless authorized by a general or specific license issued by OFAC, or exempt, OFAC’s regulations generally prohibit all transactions by U.S. persons or within (or transiting) the United States that involve any property or interests in property of blocked persons. Violations of U.S. sanctions may result in the imposition of civil or criminal penalties on U.S. and foreign persons.  OFAC may impose civil penalties for sanctions violations on a strict liability basis. OFAC’s Economic Sanctions Enforcement Guidelines provide more information regarding OFAC’s enforcement of U.S. economic sanctions.  In addition, financial institutions and other persons may risk exposure to sanctions for engaging in certain transactions or activities involving designated or otherwise blocked persons.  The prohibitions include the making of any contribution or provision of funds, goods, or services by, to, or for the benefit of any designated or blocked person, or the receipt of any contribution or provision of funds, goods, or services from any such person. Furthermore, engaging in certain transactions involving the persons designated today may risk the imposition of secondary sanctions on participating foreign financial institutions.  OFAC can prohibit or impose strict conditions on opening or maintaining, in the United States, a correspondent account or a payable-through account of a foreign financial institution that knowingly conducts or facilitates any significant transaction on behalf of a person who is designated pursuant to the relevant authority. The power and integrity of OFAC sanctions derive not only from OFAC’s ability to designate and add persons to the Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List (SDN List), but also from its willingness to remove persons from the SDN List consistent with the law.  The ultimate goal of sanctions is not to punish, but to bring about a positive change in behavior.  For information concerning the process for seeking removal from an OFAC list, including the SDN List, or to submit a request, please refer to OFAC’s guidance on Filing a Petition for Removal from an OFAC List . title: Treasury Targets Cyber Scam Operators and Armed Group Facilitators in Southeast Asia
body: November 19, 2026 WASHINGTON —Today, the U.S. Department of the Treasury’s Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) sanctioned three individuals involved in operating and facilitating cyber scam centers in Southeast Asia, as well as two affiliated companies.  The individuals designated today include operators of scam compounds that target Americans through virtual currency investment fraud and affiliates of armed groups that provide protection and support to scam-center networks in Southeast Asia. “Under President Trump’s leadership, Treasury has aggressively targeted overseas scam compounds to protect Americans from fraud,” said Secretary of the Treasury Scott Bessent .  “We will continue to use all available tools to disrupt and dismantle the networks that enable scam compounds to operate.” These actions are being taken in furtherance of President Trump’s Executive Order (E.O.) 14390 of March 6, 2026, “Combating Cybercrime, Fraud, and Predatory Schemes Against American Citizens,” which orders the U.S. Government to unleash every available tool to stop foreign-backed criminal networks that exploit vulnerable Americans through cybercrime, cyber-enabled fraud, and extortion.  Today’s action further reflects OFAC’s coordination with the Federal Bureau of Investigation’s New York Field Office, Department of Justice’s Scam Center Strike Force, and the Drug Enforcement Administration, and the Homeland Security Task Force and National Coordination Center.  OFAC is taking today’s actions pursuant to E.O. 13694, as amended by E.O. 13757, E.O. 14144, and E.O. 14306 (“E.O. 13694, as further amended”). ZHAO HUI: A SCAM CENTER OPERATOR Zhao Hui (Zhao) is a Cambodian national who leased a scam center owned by the OFAC-designated Prince Group TCO and paid protection fees to the OFAC-designated leader of the Prince Group TCO, Chen Zhi .  In addition, Zhao owned a scam compound in Cambodia independent of Prince Group TCO.  At this scam compound, Zhao was directly involved in scam operations and managed this scam compound’s leases.  This scam compound primarily targeted Americans and Europeans.  Such scam compounds conduct virtual currency investment scams.  Since Zhao has leased a scam compound and owned and operated an additional scam compound in Cambodia, he has materially assisted, sponsored, or provided financial, material, or technological support for, or goods or services to or in support of virtual cryptocurrency investment scams, an activity described in subsection 1(a)(ii) of E.O. 13694, as further amended. Zhao is being designated pursuant to E.O. 13694, as further amended, for having materially assisted, sponsored, or provided financial, material, or technological support for, or goods or services to or in support of, an activity described in subsection 1(a)(ii) of E.O. 13694, as further amended. Zhao is the chairman of the board of directors of Cambodia-based construction company Bei Fang Bo Lin Construction Decoration Co., Ltd . (Bei Fang Bo Lin) and management and consultancy company ZHZ Investment Consulting Co., Ltd. (ZHZ Investment). Bei Fang Bo Lin and ZHZ Investment are being designated pursuant to E.O. 13694, as further amended, for being owned or controlled by, or having acted or purported to act for or on behalf of, directly or indirectly, Zhao Hui. THE DKBA’S FACILITATION OF SCAM COMPOUND ACTIVITY In recent years, armed groups in Burma have transformed a strip along the Thai-Burmese border into one of the world’s highest concentrations of scam centers.  The Democratic Karen Benevolent Army (DKBA) is an ethnic armed group previously designated by OFAC for supporting cyber scam centers in Burma that target Americans using fraudulent investment schemes.  DKBA actors not only provide security for scam compounds and permit their continued operation, but also actively participate in violence against victims of human trafficking trapped inside the compounds. Since December 2025, General Saw Shwe Wah has been the commander-in-chief of the DKBA, replacing General Saw Steel , who OFAC designated in November 2025 pursuant to E.O. 13694, as further amended. Colonel Saw A One is the DKBA commander who oversees security in the Three Pagodas Pass in Karen State near the Thai border.  The region has seen expansion of new buildings intended for telecom scam operations, with many scam actors entering the area with the assistance of the DKBA, which also protects them.  Saw A One reportedly owns a plantation where scam operations occur and has contracted for scam operations. Saw Shwe Wah and Saw A One are being designated pursuant to E.O. 13694, as further amended, for being or having been leaders, officials, senior executive officers, or members of the board of directors of the DKBA, a person whose property and interests in property are blocked pursuant to E.O. 13694, as further amended. SANCTIONS IMPLICATIONS As a result of today’s action, all property and interests in property of the designated persons described above that are in the United States or in the possession or control of U.S. persons are blocked and must be reported to OFAC.  In addition, any entities that are owned, directly or indirectly, individually or in the aggregate, 50 percent or more by one or more blocked persons are also blocked.  Unless authorized by a general or specific license issued by OFAC, or exempt, OFAC’s regulations generally prohibit all transactions by U.S.  persons or within (or transiting) the United States that involve any property or interests in property of designated or otherwise blocked persons. Violations of U.S. sanctions may result in the imposition of civil or criminal penalties on U.S. and foreign persons.  OFAC may impose civil penalties for sanctions violations on a strict liability basis.  OFAC’s Economic Sanctions Enforcement Guidelines provide more information regarding OFAC’s enforcement of U.S. economic sanctions.  In addition, financial institutions and other persons may risk exposure to sanctions for engaging in certain transactions or activities involving designated or otherwise blocked persons.  The prohibitions include the making of any contribution or provision of funds, goods, or services by, to, or for the benefit of any designated or blocked person, or the receipt of any contribution or provision of funds, goods, or services from any such person.  Non-U.S. persons are also prohibited from causing or conspiring to cause U.S. persons to wittingly or unwittingly violate U.S. sanctions, as well as engaging in conduct that evades U.S. sanctions.  Individuals located in the U.S. or abroad who provide information about sanctions violations to FinCEN’s whistleblower incentive program may be eligible for awards if the information they provide leads to a successful enforcement action that results in monetary penalties exceeding $1,000,000. The power and integrity of OFAC sanctions derive not only from OFAC’s ability to designate and add persons to the SDN List, but also from its willingness to remove persons from the SDN List, when consistent with relevant statutes and other authorities.   The ultimate goal of sanctions is to bring about a positive change in behavior.  What constitutes a sufficient change in circumstance will vary based on context, including the status of the broader geopolitical circumstances affecting the national security and foreign policy interests implicated by the declared national emergency. For more information concerning the process for seeking removal from an OFAC list, including the SDN List, or to submit a request, please refer to OFAC’s guidance on How to Request Removal from an OFAC List . body: Building the right way: Lessons from 20 years in The Dalles Nov 19, 2026 | x.com Facebook LinkedIn Mail Copy link We’re celebrating the 20th anniversary of our first data center in The Dalles, Oregon. Katy Bowman, Community Development Manager in The Dalles, reflects on twenty years of operating our first data center in Oregon. We have invested over $7 billion in the region, supported local schools and fire services, and created thousands of jobs. By prioritizing water conservation, carbon-free energy, and community grants, we aim to be a responsible neighbor. We look forward to continuing this partnership and supporting the local economy for many years to come. Summaries were generated by Google AI. Generative AI is experimental. Explore other styles: General summary Bullet points Basic explainer In 2006, Google opened its first owned and operated data center in The Dalles, Ore. At the time, we didn't know whether it would grow beyond two small buildings with a few servers, let alone become the digital foundation for hospitals, banks, retailers, and other businesses in the region (and across the country). Today, many of the innovations that shape how we approach data centers began there. As we mark this twenty-year milestone, we're reflecting on what we've built together with the local community, as well as what comes next. Growing alongside Wasco County Over these past two decades, Google has invested more than $7 billion in Oregon. As Wasco County's largest taxpayer in recent years, we help fund services like North Wasco County School District and Mid-Columbia Fire and Rescue. Throughout our time in Oregon, we’ve remained active members of the community: Googlers have volunteered more than 28,000 hours with nonprofits and schools around Oregon, while Google and its employees have given more than $35 million to organizations and nonprofits across the state. In addition, for many families, our presence has meant building a career without leaving home. Over the last three years, our operations have supported an average of $862 million in state GDP each year. Our workforce in The Dalles spans a variety of backgrounds and includes a father-son duo, a pair of sisters, and many employees who have been with us for more than 15 years. Googlers participate in a volunteer clean-up along The Dalles Riverfront Trail and Taylor Lake - 2025 Building the right way Since we started building in The Dalles, we’ve worked to set the industry standard in developing data centers the right way. This means paying our own way, working to keep energy affordable, creating local jobs, showing up as active participants in our communities, and protecting shared resources like power and water. Since 2022, our data centers in The Dalles have achieved more than 80% carbon-free energy — which we’re continuing to support through our 100 MW wind agreement with Avangrid and our 50 MW “superhot” geothermal deal with Quaise . We’ve also partnered with the Oregon Hazards Lab on wildfire prevention and Columbia Gorge Food Bank (CGFB) on hunger relief programs. We recirculate cooling water at least 10 times before it leaves our facilities, so every gallon goes further — leaving more for farms, families, and businesses that share the watershed. In the last three years, we’ve spent more than $38 million on local water infrastructure and replenishment projects. This includes $28 million in funding for water and sewer infrastructure and an aquifer storage and recovery (ASR) system — a project that functions like an underground water savings account for the city. Upon completion, we transferred the ASR system and associated groundwater rights to the City of The Dalles. And we developed our third campus at a former Superfund site, previously home to an old aluminum smelter, which now provides a source of jobs and tax revenue for the county. Looking ahead To commemorate the anniversary, we're announcing two new programs in support of The Dalles: 20 for 20: Throughout 2027, we'll award $20,000 grants to 20 different organizations across Wasco County — one for each year we've called The Dalles home. These grants are not only our “thank you” to the local community, but also our commitment to continue supporting local organizations that help the region thrive. Energy Impact Fund: We're also launching a $10 million Energy Impact Fund to support energy affordability and efficiency for residents of the Columbia Gorge, with the first grant going to Energy Trust of Oregon. Communities across the country are asking what it means to have a data center as a decades-long neighbor. The Dalles offers some insight: two small buildings became thousands of supported jobs, a lasting source of public revenue, and a local neighbor that is part of a thriving business community. To the people of The Dalles and Wasco County: a sincere thank you for having us as neighbors for the past 20 years. We're grateful for what we've built here, and we're committed to building responsibly together in the years ahead. Main Menu Toggle Button Sections Search Toggle Button Search Search Submit Button Submit Home News & Events Speeches Speech PDF November 19, 2026 Monetary Policy amid Frequent and Complex Shocks Vice Chair Philip N. Jefferson At the International Monetary Fund and Central Bank of Brazil Conference “A Quarter Century of Inflation Targeting in Latin America:  Progress, Challenges, and the Road Ahead,” Brasília, Brazil Share Watch Live Thank you, Nigel, for that kind introduction, and thank you to the Central Bank of Brazil and International Monetary Fund for hosting this important conference. 1 It is an honor to be here with my fellow panelists. Today, I will briefly discuss issues that are critical for central bankers around the world—that is, how to assess and confront economic shocks. I discussed these issues in more depth in a speech earlier this year at Stanford University. 2 Shocks, by their nature, are difficult to predict and vary in length, but we are nonetheless very familiar with them. Just in the past few years, we have experienced a pandemic, a rapid rise in energy prices associated with geopolitical tensions, changes to trade policy, and a technological breakthrough. One way to classify shocks is to determine whether their initial effect is on the demand side or the supply side of the economy. Demand shocks affect spending by households, businesses, or the government without changing productive capacity. Supply shocks change productive capacity—what economists call "potential output"—by affecting the available supply of labor and capital or the productivity of those inputs. The nature and duration of these shocks influence the approach to monetary policymaking. As a monetary policymaker in the United States, I must consider whether and how shocks impact both sides of our dual mandate—maximum employment and stable prices. When a shock moves the output gap and inflation in the same direction, our objectives are aligned, and policy actions taken to address one also support the other. 3 When a shock pushes them in opposite directions, there is a tradeoff. The recent rise in oil prices tied to the conflict in the Middle East is an example of the latter. An energy price shock can push up inflation while weighing on real incomes and demand. The appropriate response depends on the relative costs of missing each objective and the balance of risks. When the recent energy price shock occurred, inflation in the U.S. was already above our 2 percent target. If inflation expectations risk becoming unanchored, a stronger reaction to inflation is warranted. If price pressures are contained, it may be prudent to prioritize downside risks to employment. Shocks that affect both aggregate supply and aggregated demand but with differential timing are especially challenging for monetary policymakers. The rapid adoption of artificial intelligence (AI) represents such a shock. Business adoption of AI has risen considerably over the past two years. 4 On the demand side, optimism about the technology has been boosting business investment in data centers, advanced computing equipment, and related products. On the supply side, AI is likely to automate some tasks and augment others, which could raise productivity and, in turn, the growth rate of potential output. Currently, the AI buildout is exerting upward pressure on demand and inflation. In the future, advancements in productivity could exert downward pressure on inflation while continuing to support growth. Labor market effects are relevant as well. AI could cause some job displacement, a meaningful challenge for affected households. Like many technological breakthroughs of the past, however, AI could lead to the creation of new jobs and new firms that we have not yet imagined. Shocks do not arrive in a vacuum. Energy, trade, and AI shocks are all unfolding at once. My colleagues at the Fed and my peers around the world must weigh them simultaneously. Our task is to remain attentive to our respective mandates and to keep the stance of our policies appropriately calibrated to achieve those stated goals. For the U.S. economy, my goal is to restore price stability while maintaining a solid labor market. That outcome will help the economy grow according to its full potential. Thank you, and I look forward to our discussion. 1. The views expressed here are my own and are not necessarily those of my colleagues on the Federal Open Market Committee or the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System. Return to text 2. See Philip N. Jefferson, " Navigating Economic Shocks: A Monetary Policymaker's Perspective ," speech delivered at the Stanford Institute for Economic Policy Research, Stanford University, Stanford, CA, July 16, 2026. Return to text 3. The output gap is the difference between the economy's actual output, typically measured by GDP, and an estimate of its potential output. A positive gap signals excess demand, with employment above its maximum sustainable level and upward pressure on inflation; a negative gap signals excess supply, with the opposite effects. Return to text 4. Recent technological advancements discussed in this speech are sometimes referred to as super intelligence or SI. Return to text Last Update:

title: Season’s Streamings and Savings: Black Friday Deals Come to GeForce NOW
body: Season’s Streamings and Savings: Black Friday Deals Come to GeForce NOW Plus, bring PC gaming to more Fire TV Stick devices with a special sale, and stream five Bethesda favorites from GOG as part of nine games this week. November 19, 2026 by GeForce NOW Community 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! GeForce NOW is kicking off Black Friday with more reasons to make time for gaming. Six-month memberships are back for a limited time. Save 30% on the first six-month term of a Performance or Ultimate membership . Big gaming plans, smaller price tag. Keep the holiday savings going: Check out more NVIDIA holiday deals for gamers, creators and AI enthusiasts. The living room gets a little more playtime, too. GeForce NOW arrives on Amazon Fire TV Stick HD, Fire TV Stick 4K Select and Fire TV Stick 4K (2026 model) running Vega OS, alongside an Amazon offer launching later today for 90% off the first month of an eligible Performance or Ultimate membership in participating countries. It brings console-style gaming to the TV, straight from the Amazon cart. Bethesda fans have more in store, with five favorites adding GOG support as part of nine games joining GeForce NOW this week. Big RTX Power, Black Friday Price Thousands of games are calling from the cloud. Six-month Performance and Ultimate memberships are back for Black Friday, with 30% off the first six months for new memberships and eligible upgrades in select regions. The sale runs through Monday, Nov. 30, while supplies last. Go Ultimate for GeForce RTX 5080-class performance across PCs, Macs, Steam Deck and other supported handhelds, browsers, mobile devices, compatible TVs and more . Sessions lasting up to eight hours and first-priority server access leave more room for marathon play. Ultimate brings the latest NVIDIA innovations to the cloud, including DLSS 5 technology with the 3D-Guided Neural Rendering feature for lifelike lighting and materials in NBA 2K27 and Hogwarts Legacy , with support coming to War Thunder and Where Winds Meet . The experience goes big with streaming at up to 5K resolution or up to 360 frames per second, plus high dynamic range, ultrawide support and saved in-game settings. DLSS Super Resolution, Multi Frame Generation and Ray Reconstruction enhance supported games, including the path-traced missions of 007 First Light and the reality-bending action of CONTROL Resonant , while NVIDIA Reflex and Cloud G-SYNC technologies help keep gameplay responsive and smooth. GeForce NOW handles downloads, patches and updates for Ready-to-Play games, freeing local storage and leaving more time for gaming. Choose a membership and start the season streaming. More Screens, Major Savings Press play on more possibilities. GeForce NOW officially expands to all three of Amazon’s Vega OS streaming media players including Fire TV Stick HD, Fire TV Stick 4K Select and Fire TV Stick 4K (2026 model) bringing thousands of supported games to more another screens in the home. Vega OS keeps Fire TV fast and responsive, so launching GeForce NOW and jumping into games feels quick and snappy, with no console required. Getting started is simple: download the GeForce NOW app on a supported Fire TV device , sign in and connect a compatible controller. From cozy stories to epic adventures, turn-based tactics to co-op challenges, there’s plenty to build, explore and share with friends — all from the comfort of the couch. There’s a fire deal to get the games going, too. Launching later today through Thursday, Dec. 31, get 90% off the first month of a Performance or Ultimate membership purchased directly through Amazon on supported Fire TV devices in participating regions. The cloud is ready. The next quest is calling. GOG Big or Go Home Five favorite worlds. Extra ways to play. Five Bethesda titles expand their GeForce NOW support this week with their GOG versions: Indiana Jones and the Great Circle , Fallout 4 , The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim , DOOM and DOOM Eternal . Uncover an ancient mystery in Indiana Jones and the Great Circle , a first-person adventure set between Raiders of the Lost Ark and The Last Crusade . Explore the wasteland in Fallout 4 or trade the Pip-Boy for dragons and open-world fantasy in The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim . For a faster change of pace, DOOM brings relentless enemies, destructive weapons and fast-moving first-person combat, while its sequel, DOOM Eternal , turns up the intensity as the Slayer takes on demonic forces. Members who own the newly supported GOG versions can stream those titles through GeForce NOW without purchasing them again. From treasure hunts to dragon hunts, the collection can follow across nearly any supported device. Familiar worlds, with a little more room to roam. Members can look for the following games joining the GeForce NOW library this week: Volvy’s Adventure: Reslimed (New release on Steam , Nov. 19) Baldur’s Gate 3 ( Xbox Play Anywhere) DOOM (2016) ( GOG ) DOOM Eternal ( GOG ) Fallout 4 ( GOG ) Graveyard Keeper 2 ( Epic Games Store and GOG ) Indiana Jones and the Great Circle ( GOG ) Moon Sweepers ( Steam ) The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim Anniversary Edition ( GOG ) Dates listed above reflect when games are released on their respective stores. GeForce NOW availability may vary, as games are onboarded after release and added throughout the week. Keep an eye on GeForce NOW channels and GFN Thursdays for availability updates on announced titles. Make it a cloud gaming weekend. Grab a day pass to try Performance or Ultimate before committing to a monthly membership, with the day pass cost applicable toward that first month. What’s on the big-screen gaming lineup this weekend? Let us know on X or in the comments below. title: We’re partnering with Blue Origin on our first heavy-lift Project Suncatcher launch.
body: We’re partnering with Blue Origin on our first heavy-lift Project Suncatcher launch. Travis Beals Senior Director, Paradigms of Intelligence Nov 19, 2026 We’re partnering with Blue Origin on the first heavy-lift launch for Project Suncatcher, our long-term moonshot to scale AI infrastructure in space by tapping into the abundant solar power in orbit. Targeted for Q1 2029, Blue Origin’s heavy-lift New Glenn rocket will deploy our satellites — each with roughly the capacity of a data center rack — into sun-synchronous orbit. This dedicated launch builds on our ongoing work with other satellite and launch partners and represents a crucial milestone on our long-term roadmap as we expand the boundaries of what's possible for the future of compute.

title: Pulaski County Man Sentenced for Armed Methamphetamine Trafficking
body: Press Release Pulaski County Man Sentenced for Armed Methamphetamine Trafficking Thursday, November 19, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Eastern District of Kentucky LONDON, Ky. – A Somerset, Ky., man, Matthew Tunnat, 34, was sentenced on Wednesday to 18 years in prison by U.S. District Judge Robert Wier for possession with intent to distribute controlled substances, including 50 grams or more of methamphetamine and cocaine, and possession of a firearm in furtherance of a drug trafficking crime. On October 15, 2025, law enforcement conducted a traffic stop on a vehicle being driven by Tunnat. Law enforcement located $2,524 in cash on Tunnat and a backpack in the car that contained 449.27 grams of methamphetamine and two bags of cocaine. The methamphetamine was packaged for resale in several different plastic bags that were wrapped in labels that read “Thank You for Supporting My Local Business.” During the same search, law enforcement also found a loaded firearm in the center console. At the time of the traffic stop, the firearm was easily accessible to Tunnat and was in close proximity to him and the methamphetamine. Tunnat admitted to possessing the firearm to protect himself and his drug trafficking proceeds. As a convicted felon, Tunnat was also prohibited from possessing a firearm. Jason Parman, United States Attorney for the Eastern District of Kentucky; Jim Scott, Special Agent in Charge, DEA, Louisville Field Division, jointly announced the sentence. The investigation was conducted by the DEA and Laurel County Sheriff’s Office. Assistant U.S. Attorney Drew Trimble prosecuted the case on behalf of the United States. – END – Contact CONTACT:  Jenny Parker PHONE:  (859) 685-4906 E-MAIL: jenny.parker@usdoj.gov Updated November 19, 2026 Topics Drug Trafficking Firearms Offenses Component USAO - Kentucky, Eastern

title: Stockton man indicted for possessing 16,000 carfentanil-laced pills, 57 pounds of methamphetamine, and 13 firearms
body: Press Release Stockton man indicted for possessing 16,000 carfentanil-laced pills, 57 pounds of methamphetamine, and 13 firearms Thursday, November 19, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Eastern District of California SACRAMENTO, Calif. — A federal grand jury returned a three-count indictment today against Peter Anthony Zile, 60, of Stockton, charging him with possession with intent to distribute methamphetamine and carfentanil and with being a felon in possession of a firearm, U.S. Attorney Eric Grant announced. According to court documents, officers on the Delta Regional Auto Theft Team (RATT) found a stolen Ford F-350 parked in the driveway of Zile’s residence. During the execution of a search warrant at the residence, officers seized approximately 57 pounds of crystal methamphetamine, 13 firearms, several high-capacity magazines, approximately 4,390 rounds of ammunition, and more than $250,000 in cash. Agents also seized approximately 16,000 counterfeit M30 pills containing carfentanil, a dangerous synthetic opioid related to fentanyl. Zile is in custody pending trial. He is prohibited from possessing firearms or ammunition because of prior felony convictions including stalking, possession of a controlled substance for sale, and elder abuse. Homeland Security Investigations, the California Highway Patrol, the Stockton Police Department, and the San Joaquin County Sheriff’s Office conducted the investigation. Assistant U.S. Attorney Charles Campbell is prosecuting the case. If convicted, Zile faces a maximum statutory penalty of life years in prison, a mandatory minimum of 10 years in prison, and a $10 million fine. Any sentence, however, would be determined at the discretion of the court after consideration of any applicable statutory factors and the federal Sentencing Guidelines, which take into account a number of variables. The charges are only allegations; the defendant is presumed innocent until and unless proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt. Updated November 19, 2026 Topics Drug Trafficking Firearms Offenses Component USAO - California, Eastern

title: Alabama Man Sentenced for Role in False Distress Hoax
body: Press Release Alabama Man Sentenced for Role in False Distress Hoax Thursday, November 19, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Eastern District of Louisiana brittany.t.maique@usdoj.gov NEW ORLEANS , LOUISIANA – Seth Emde , age 23, of Alabama, was sentenced on November 18, 2026, for his role in a scheme to stage the death of his father, Melvin Emde, and trigger a false United States Coast Guard search-and-rescue operation, announced United States Attorney David I. Courcelle. According to court documents, in August 2023, Seth Emde helped carry out a scheme to make authorities believe that his father, Melvin Emde, had drowned in the Mississippi River, allowing him to evade prosecution in North Carolina for a pending sex offense involving a minor. As part of the scheme, the conspirators purchased fishing equipment and kayaks and placed them along the banks of the Mississippi River in St. Charles Parish, Louisiana, to create the false appearance that Melvin Emde had disappeared while fishing. After Melvin Emde removed his court-ordered ankle monitor and went into hiding, Seth Emde placed a false distress call to the United States Coast Guard reporting that his father was missing. The call prompted a large-scale search-and-rescue operation involving federal, state, and local resources. Melvin Emde was later located in Georgia living under an assumed name. United States District Judge Greg Gerard Guidry sentenced Seth Emde to three years of probation and ordered him to pay $95,397 in restitution to the United States Coast Guard for costs incurred during the search operation. U.S. Attorney Courcelle praised the work of the United States Coast Guard, including the Coast Guard Investigative Service, and the St. Charles Parish Sheriff's Office. Assistant United States Attorney Spiro G. Latsis of the General Crimes Unit prosecuted the case. Contact Brittany Maique Executive Assistant U.S. Attorney's Office Eastern District of Louisiana Updated November 19, 2026 Component USAO - Louisiana, Eastern

title: Clinton Man Arrested and Charged With Being a Felon in Possession of a Firearm
body: Press Release Clinton Man Arrested and Charged With Being a Felon in Possession of a Firearm Thursday, November 19, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Massachusetts BOSTON – A previously convicted felon has been arrested for allegedly possessing a firearm. Todd Brandt, 46, of Clinton, Mass. has been charged with being a felon in possession of a firearm. Brandt was arrested yesterday and, following an initial appearance in federal court in Boston, remains detained pending a hearing scheduled for Nov. 23, 2026. According to the charging document, on July 15, 2026, Brandt allegedly possessed a firearm in Worcester. Brandt was previously convicted of felonies punishable by more than one year in prison, including: uttering a false prescription, obtaining a drug through fraud and forgery of a document in Barnstable District Court and assault and battery with a dangerous weapon in Leominster District Court. The charge of being a felon in possession of a firearm provides for a sentence of up to 15 years in prison, three years of supervised release and a fine of up to $250,000. Sentences are imposed by a federal district court judge based upon the U.S. Sentencing Guidelines and statutes which govern the determination of a sentence in a criminal case. United States Attorney Leah B. Foley and Thomas Greco, Special Agent in Charge of the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms & Explosives, Boston Field Division made the announcement. Valuable assistance was provided by the Clinton Police Department. Assistant U.S. Attorney Brendan O’Shea of the Worcester Branch Office is prosecuting the case. The details contained in the charging document are allegations. The defendant is presumed to be innocent unless and until proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt in the court of law. title: 15 Members And Associates Of Gorilla Stone Bloods Gang Charged With Narcotics And Firearms Offenses In Sara D. Roosevelt Park
body: Press Release 15 Members And Associates Of Gorilla Stone Bloods Gang Charged With Narcotics And Firearms Offenses In Sara D. Roosevelt Park Thursday, November 19, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Southern District of New York United States Attorney for the Southern District of New York, Jamie McDonald, Acting Special Agent in Charge of the New York Field Office of Homeland Security Investigations (“HSI”), Pete Gizas, Special Agent in Charge of the New York Task Force Division of the Drug Enforcement Administration (“DEA”), Christopher Roberts, and Commissioner of the New York City Police Department (“NYPD”), Jessica S. Tisch, announced today the unsealing of an Indictment charging 15 members and associates of the Untouchable Gorilla Stone Nation (“Gorilla Stone”), a set of the nationwide Bloods street gang, with conspiring to distribute crack cocaine, heroin, fentanyl, and synthetic cannabinoids in and around Sara D. Roosevelt Park (“SDR Park”) in the Lower East Side of Manhattan.  Some defendants were additionally charged with possessing firearms, some of which were brandished and discharged, in furtherance of their narcotics trafficking.  Six of the defendants were in New York City or New York State custody and brought into federal custody, with eight of the remaining nine defendants arrested and presented in federal court.  The case is assigned to U.S. District Judge Lewis J. Liman. “Our Office will stop at nothing to keep New Yorkers and our community safe,” said U.S. Attorney Jamie McDonald.  “This is particularly true for public spaces in New York, like our parks. As alleged, for years a violent gang network operated an open-air drug market that poisoned the Lower East Side of Manhattan with fentanyl, heroin, crack cocaine, and K2.  The defendants allegedly trafficked deadly drugs while arming themselves with illegal firearms and engaging in brutal violence to protect their turf.  Gang-driven narcotics trafficking inflicts enormous harm on neighborhoods and families. New Yorkers should know that they can count on our Office and our law enforcement partners to protect them from these harms.” “Today’s arrests strike a major blow against this gang who is accused of using fear, violence, narcotics sales, and illegal guns to control the streets and parks of a New York City community,” said HSI Acting Special Agent in Charge Pete Gizas.  “New Yorkers deserve safe neighborhoods, not ones ruled by violent criminal organizations.  We will combat these violent gangs with decisive law enforcement might.  HSI New York, alongside the U.S. Attorney’s Office, NYPD, DEA, and all our law enforcement partners, will relentlessly pursue those responsible and hold them accountable.” “All New Yorkers deserve the right to live, work, and enjoy public spaces and parks free from drugs, gangs, and violence,” said DEA New York Task Force Division Special Agent in Charge Christopher Roberts.  “These defendants allegedly turned the Sara D. Roosevelt Park into an open-air drug market, using fear, intimidation, and brutal violence to control areas of the park and terrorize this community.  From vicious slashings and stabbings to shootings and armed assaults, these violent acts demonstrated the dangerous lengths these individuals used to protect their criminal enterprise and exert control over our neighborhoods.  Today, those days are over!  The DEA and our law enforcement partners will not stand idle while violent gangs attempt to take over our parks and neighborhoods.  Our public spaces belong to the people, not drug traffickers and criminals.” “As alleged, these defendants, part of the Untouchable Gorilla Stone Nation gang, turned a Lower East Side park into their own open-air drug market and violent playground,” said NYPD Commissioner Jessica S. Tisch.  “This takedown is yet another example of the diligent work our investigators do to dismantle dangerous gangs and stop the illegal drug businesses that threaten our communities.  I thank our dedicated NYPD detectives, law enforcement partners, and the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Southern District of New York for their shared commitment to making New York City safer.” According to the Indictment and public court filings:(1) Between approximately 2023 and 2026, the defendants were members or associates of the Gorilla Stone gang and took over SDR Park, in the heart of the Lower East Side, with violence and fear through the trafficking of crack cocaine, heroin, fentanyl, and synthetic cannabinoids or K2.  The defendants had established agreements, understandings, and practices that governed how they operated and how their different members coexisted within the same drug-dealing territory.  For example, the defendants divided SDR Park, with certain dealers controlling different parts of the Park.  While these dealers permitted one another to sell in close physical proximity, they did not allow outsiders or newcomers to sell in their territory and worked together, often using violence to keep out rival or unfamiliar drug dealers.  The defendants also exercised control over the Park by working in shifts.  By agreement and with proactive coordination, certain dealers, along with their workers, sold in the morning, while others sold in the evening or overnight.  In addition, the defendants warned each other about law enforcement’s presence in the area, shared suppliers (and several defendants and other members of the conspiracy themselves supplied narcotics to other defendants), steered customers to each other, provided each other with narcotics when someone ran out, and jointly responded to threats that might impact any dealer in SDR Park. To protect and further its drug business, certain of the defendants engaged in frequent acts of violence, including committing slashings, stabbings, robberies, and gun violence against rival drug dealers in the area and their own narcotics customers, typically drug-addicted individuals.  For instance: In December 2024, in the vicinity of SDR Park, Ibrahim Toure, a/k/a “Fah,” sold K2 to a customer who paid Toure with counterfeit cash.  Toure slashed the victim twice, once to the top of his head and once to his face, as depicted below. In February 2026, in the vicinity of SDR Park, Matthew Newman, a/k/a “Money,” participated in the stabbing of a victim whose close friend had a narcotics-related debt to Newman.  Specifically, Newman gave a blade to an uncharged coconspirator, who stabbed the victim seven times in the back, resulting in a collapsed lung and bleeding from a kidney. In April 2026, in the vicinity of SDR Park, Newman, Basil Simms, a/k/a “Sheff,” Sean Sims, a/k/a “Vito,” and one unidentified perpetrator assaulted and stabbed another drug dealer who was selling K2 at under-market prices.  A photo of the victim’s leg is depicted below. In July 2026, CAMERON BARNHILL, a/k/a “Baby Ape,” and ASHANTE INNISS, a/k/a “Fire,” with other perpetrators, assaulted and robbed a competitor drug dealer near SDR Park, including by stomping on his face and neck and by beating him with a traffic cone.  A screenshot of the assault is depicted below: In May 2024, NEWMAN, with two other perpetrators, committed a gang-related assault, including a pistol-whipping, of another Gorilla Stone member who was perceived to be a disfavored member of the gang.  Screenshots of NEWMAN committing the gang assault, which took place near SDR Park, are depicted below: Several members of Gorilla Stone, including some of the defendants, also possessed and carried firearms in and around SDR Park, including to have firearms available in the event of a dispute.  For example, from approximately 2024 to 2025, Sims, then a member of another Bloods set, engaged in a series of back-and-forth acts of violence with Newman regarding, among other things, their respective drug-dealing territory and influence in SDR Park.  Following a March 2025 incident in which Newman and Sims slashed each other, Sims determined that he wanted to join Gorilla Stone to avoid continued fighting with Newman.  Newman provided Sims with a gun and told him to shoot an enemy of Gorilla Stone.  On or about April 19, 2026, Sims and an uncharged coconspirator shot a 16-year-old victim in the upper thigh, as depicted below.  The victim was hospitalized. *                *                * A chart containing the defendants’ names, charges, and maximum penalties is set forth below. The maximum potential sentences in this case are prescribed by Congress and provided here for informational purposes only, as any sentencing of the defendants will be determined by the judge. Mr. McDonald thanked HSI, DEA, and the NYPD for their exceptional investigative work, as well as the Digital Forensics Unit, and the Complex Analytics and Social Media Enhancement Team at the New York/New Jersey High Intensity Drug Trafficking Area of the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Southern District of New York.  Mr. McDonald further thanked the United States Marshals Service for their assistance and partnership. This case is being handled by the Office’s Narcotics Unit.  Assistant U.S. Attorneys Remy Grosbard, Kevin Grossinger, Mostafa Khairy, and Lauren E. Phillips are in charge of the prosecution. The charges contained in the Indictment are merely accusations, and the defendants are presumed innocent unless and until proven guilty. Charge Defendants Penalties Count One Narcotics Distribution Conspiracy (21 U.S.C. §§ 841(a)(1), 841(b)(1)(A), 841(b)(1)(C), and 846) MATTHEW NEWMAN, a/k/a “Money” SEAN SIMS, a/k/a “Vito” JAHFARI JOHNSON, a/k/a “G Dot” MICHAEL DURHAM, a/k/a “Kano” RAVELL ROSSER, a/k/a “Velle” ASHANTE INNISS, a/k/a “Fire” CAMERON BARNHILL, a/k/a “Baby Ape” TYRE BANKS, a/k/a “Mighty” BASIL SIMMS, a/k/a “Sheff” IBRAHIM TOURE, a/k/a “Fah” JADEN WAYNE, a/k/a “Six,” a/k/a “Six Shot” JOSEPH CRISPIN, a/k/a “Chance” MARVIN WARD, a/k/a “Marv” TRAYVON JOHNSON, a/k/a “Trigga” ANTONIO TORRECILLA, a/k/a “Tone” Maximum: Life in prison Count Two Firearm Use, Carrying, and Possession (18 U.S.C. §§ 924(c)(1)(A)(i), (ii), and (iii), and 2) MATTHEW NEWMAN, a/k/a “Money” SEAN SIMS, a/k/a “Vito” Maximum: Life in prison Minimum: Ten years in prison, which must be consecutive to any other term imposed. Count Three Firearm Use, Carrying, and Possession (18 U.S.C. §§ 924(c)(1)(A)(i) and 2) JAHFARI JOHNSON a/k/a “G Dot” MICHAEL DURHAM, a/k/a “Kano” RAVELL ROSSER, a/k/a “Velle” ASHANTE INNISS, a/k/a “Fire” CAMERON BARNHILL, a/k/a “Baby Ape” BASIL SIMMS, a/k/a “Sheff” IBRAHIM TOURE, a/k/a “Fah” JADEN WAYNE, a/k/a “Six,” a/k/a “Six Shot” JOSEPH CRISPIN, a/k/a “Chance” MARVIN WARD, a/k/a “Marv” Maximum: Life in prison Minimum: Five years in prison, which must be consecutive to any other term imposed. ^ As the introductory phrase signifies, the entirety of the text of the Indictment and the description of the Indictment set forth herein constitute only allegations, and every fact described therein should be treated as an allegation. title: A Total of Fourteen Illegal Aliens Sentenced to Prison in Three Separate Conspiracies and for Possessing Property Stolen from Multiple Burglaries
body: Press Release A Total of Fourteen Illegal Aliens Sentenced to Prison in Three Separate Conspiracies and for Possessing Property Stolen from Multiple Burglaries Thursday, November 19, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of New Jersey NEWARK, N.J. – Since 2025, fourteen Chilean nationals, present in the United States illegally and believed to be part of three South American theft groups, pleaded guilty and were sentenced to imprisonment for engaging in multiple conspiracies involving burglaries in New Jersey and elsewhere, U.S. Attorney Robert Frazer announced. Flavio Bladimir Astete Castillo, Dareyen Mauricio Cortes-Canete, Luis Esteban Castillo Vivar, Max Vidal Navarrete, Jordán Estefano Contreras Vilches, and Juan Jose Ramirez Nilo, all of Chile, were each charged by criminal complaint in May 2024 and each pleaded guilty to conspiracy and to possessing stolen property taken from residential burglaries, including in New Jersey, which was transported over state lines. Christofer Sanguesa Aguirre, Fabiana Prado Scatarzi, Santana Arturo Castillo Gonzalez, Felipe Andres Del Valle Munoz, Carlos Alfredo Calderon Valencia, Diego Antonio Calderon Leiva, and Pedro Alejandro Salgado Vallejos, all of Chile, were each charged by criminal complaint in January 2025 and each pleaded guilty to conspiracy and possessing stolen property taken from residential burglaries, including in New Jersey, which was transported over state lines. Gustavo Ignacio Salas Ortega, also of Chile, was charged by criminal complaint in February 2025 and pleaded guilty to conspiracy and possessing stolen property taken from a burglary of a jewelry store in New Jersey, which was transported over state lines. All of the defendants were sentenced to terms of imprisonment of between 15 and 30 months, as shown in the table below. Defendant Date of Sentence U.S. District Judge Prison Sentence Vidal Navarrete Oct. 22, 2025 Claire C. Cecchi Time served (approx. 17 months) Castillo Vivar Nov. 4, 2025 Claire C. Cecchi 27 months Contreras Vilches Nov. 13, 2025 Claire C. Cecchi 27 months Ramirez Nilo Nov. 20, 2025 Claire C. Cecchi Time served (approx. 18 months) Cortes-Canete Feb. 26, 2026 Claire C. Cecchi Time served (approx. 21 months) Astete Castillo Mar. 18, 2026 Claire C. Cecchi Time served (approx. 22 months) Del Valle Munoz Apr. 9, 2026 Christine P. O’Hearn Time served (approx. 15 months) Prado Scatarzi Apr. 13, 2026 Christine P. O’Hearn Time served (approx. 15 months) Sanguesa Aguirre June 2, 2026 Christine P. O’Hearn Time served (approx. 16 months) Salgado Vallejos June 8, 2026 Christine P. O’Hearn Time served (approx. 17 months) Castillo Gonzalez June 18, 2026 Christine P. O’Hearn 22 months Salas Ortega Oct. 26, 2026 Michael A. Shipp 30 months Calderon Leiva Nov. 17, 2026 Christine P. O’Hearn 21 months Calderon Valencia Nov. 17, 2026 Christine P. O’Hearn 27 months “These fourteen defendants engaged in sophisticated, highly organized burglaries that targeted residences and businesses in New Jersey and beyond.  They did significant damage to the victims’ lives, invaded their private spaces, and put the public in danger. My office and our law enforcement partners are committed to finding perpetrators like these and preventing them from harming innocent people in New Jersey and across the United States.” - U.S. Attorney Robert Frazer “By design, these criminal tourists left behind very few clues when committing these burglaries. They used their nomadic lifestyle to cloak their identities and movements, believing it would help them evade detection,” said FBI Special Agent in Charge Stefanie Roddy.  “What they could not have foreseen was the determination of the agents and task force officers assigned to the Newark FBI Joint Organized Crime Task Force, who meticulously gathered evidence and collaborated with partners across the country. To other thieves who operate in the same way: justice will find you.” “Fourteen Chilean nationals who were unlawfully present in the United States preyed on law-abiding Americans by participating in organized burglary and theft schemes that targeted residences, businesses, and valuable property across New Jersey and beyond,” said ICE-ERO Acting Field Office Director Tammy Marich. “After entering and remaining in this country in violation of our immigration laws, they demonstrated a calculated disregard for the people they victimized, the safety of our communities, and the rule of law. ICE Enforcement and Removal Operations Newark remains committed to identifying, arresting, and removing criminal illegal aliens who exploit law-abiding members of our communities.” According to documents filed in this case and statements made in court: Astete Castillo, Cortes-Canete, Castillo Vivar, Vidal Navarrete, Contreras Vilches, and Ramirez Nilo were part of a burglary ring that committed multiple residential burglaries in March and April 2024 in multiple states, including New Jersey, Maryland, and New York. The defendants stole large amounts of jewelry, collectibles, and other valuables from the residences. Sanguesa Aguirre, Prado Scatarzi, Castillo Gonzalez, Del Valle Munoz, Calderon Valencia, Calderon Leiva, and Salgado Vallejos were part of a sophisticated burglary ring that committed multiple residential burglaries in November 2024 in New Jersey and Massachusetts.  The defendants broke into homes, stole jewelry, watches, designer handbags, and other valuable goods, and then traveled with them to other states. At the scene of one burglary, in Massachusetts, the defendants destroyed precious keepsakes that included the cremated remains of a loved one, which the residents had stored in their home. The defendants also used signal jamming devices to interfere with security alarm systems while committing the burglaries. When several of the defendants were arrested by immigration authorities in November 2024, Del Valle Munoz and Calderon Valencia fled across the country, eventually appearing near Seattle, Washington before traveling to a residence in Carlton, Oregon. Law enforcement searched the residence where Del Valle Munoz, Calderon Valencia, and others had arrived and recovered bags and backpacks containing additional gold jewelry, diamonds, and watches, along with burglary tools and jamming devices. Castillo Gonzalez also pleaded guilty and was sentenced for possessing a contraband cell phone after he was arrested and pending trial in a detention facility used to house federal detainees. Salas Ortega was part of a third group that scouted a jewelry store in a New Jersey mall before committing a burglary of the jewelry store by cutting a hole through an adjacent wall. The group also used a wireless security camera to watch for security guards while they committed the burglary. Law enforcement later found Salas Ortega wearing an expensive wristwatch that had been in the jewelry store at the time of the burglary. The defendant was seen on surveillance cameras wearing the stolen wristwatch in New York on multiple days after the burglary. In addition to the prison terms, Judge Cecci, Judge Shipp, and Judge O’Hearn each ordered the respective defendants to pay restitution to the victims of the conspiracies. The restitution judgments totaled $2,591,323.82. U.S. Attorney Frazer credited the FBI Newark’s Joint Organized Crime Task Force (JOCTF), under the direction of Special Agent in Charge Stefanie Roddy in Newark; Immigration and Customs Enforcement – Enforcement and Removal Operations, under the direction of Field Office Director Tammy Marich; the Millburn Police Department under the direction of Chief Brian Gilfedder; the Clinton Township Police Department, under the direction of Chief Thomas A. DeRosa, and the Denver Police Department, under the direction of Chief Ron Thomas, with the investigations leading to the sentences. He also thanked the Port Authority of New York and New Jersey Police Department, Warren Township Police Department, Amtrak Police Department, Baltimore County Police Burglary Unit, Jersey City Police Department, Los Angeles Police Department, New York State Police, Westchester County Police, NJ Transit Police, Colts Neck Police Department, Keansburg Police Department, Fort Lee Police Department, Paramus Police Department, New Jersey State Police, Spring Valley Police Department (NY), Town of Greenburgh Police Department (NY), Wellesley Police Department (MA), Westwood Police Department (MA), Massachusetts State Police, Renton Police Department (WA), King County Sheriff’s Office (WA), Tukwila Police Department (WA), Oregon State Police, Yamhill County Sheriff’s Office (OR), Carlton Police Department (OR), Pennsylvania State Police, Novi Police Department (MI), Denver District Attorney’s Office, Essex County Prosecutor’s Office, Monmouth County Prosecutor’s Office, ICE/ERO Portland, ICE/ERO Seattle, U.S. Customs and Border Protection, FBI Denver, FBI New York, FBI Philadelphia, FBI Seattle, FBI Portland, FBI New Orleans, FBI Boston, FBI Los Angeles, DEA Newark, Policía de Investigaciones de Chile (PDI), and the FBI Legal Attaché Santiago, Chile. Finally, U.S. Attorney Frazer thanked the Jewelers’ Security Alliance for its support of the investigations. The government is represented by Assistant U.S. Attorney Trevor A. Chenoweth of the Cybercrime Unit in Newark. ### Defense counsel: Flavio Bladimir Astete Castillo: Maximillian Novel Esq., Jersey City, New Jersey Dareyen Mauricio Cortes-Canete: Michael T. title: Mexican National Unlawfully Residing in the United States Sentenced to More Than Three Years in Federal Prison for Trafficking Fentanyl
body: Press Release Mexican National Unlawfully Residing in the United States Sentenced to More Than Three Years in Federal Prison for Trafficking Fentanyl Thursday, November 19, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Oregon PORTLAND, Ore. — A Mexican national unlawfully residing in the United States was sentenced to 41 months in federal prison and five years of supervised release for possessing more than 1.5 kilograms of fentanyl with intent to distribute, U.S. Attorney Scott E. Bradford announced. Mario De La Paz Aguilar , 29, a citizen of Mexico living in Portland, is expected to face immigration proceedings and removal from the United States after completing his prison sentence. “Fentanyl continues to devastate families and communities across Oregon,” said U.S. Attorney Scott E. Bradford . “Individuals who unlawfully remain in the United States and engage in large-scale drug trafficking will be prosecuted and held accountable for the harm they cause.” According to court documents, on April 24, 2026, Portland Police Bureau officers responded to a report of a disturbance at a residence in Southeast Portland. During the investigation, officers learned Aguilar was involved in fentanyl distribution and obtained information that narcotics were being stored at the residence. A subsequent search of the residence resulted in the seizure of approximately 1,720 gross grams of fentanyl, including powder and fentanyl packaged in brick form. Investigators also recovered drug-packaging materials, scales, a food-sealing machine, a ledger, a gas mask, multiple bags of mannitol, a substance commonly used as a cutting agent, and approximately $4,000 in cash. After his arrest, Aguilar admitted the fentanyl belonged to him and acknowledged participating in its distribution. He also told investigators he had traveled to California to obtain narcotics for distribution in Oregon. Aguilar pleaded guilty Aug. 18, 2026, to possession with intent to distribute fentanyl. The case was investigated by the Portland Police Bureau and Homeland Security Investigations. The case was prosecuted by Assistant U.S. Attorney Cassady A. Adams. ### Updated November 19, 2026 Topic Drug Trafficking Component USAO - Oregon

title: Billings man sentenced to 9 years in prison for trafficking fentanyl from home
body: Press Release Billings man sentenced to 9 years in prison for trafficking fentanyl from home Thursday, November 19, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Montana BILLINGS – A Billings man who trafficked significant amounts of fentanyl from his West End home was sentenced today to nine years in prison, followed by four years of supervised release, U.S. Attorney Scott Twito said. U.S. District Judge Kathleen S. Lane presided. Jason Allen Lehman, 50, pleaded guilty in July 2026 to possession with intent to distribute fentanyl and possession of a firearm in furtherance of a drug trafficking crime. The government alleged in court documents that Lehman had been using the postal service to obtain fentanyl pills, which he then trafficked around Billings from his home on the West End. The investigation into Lehman began on Feb. 24, 2025, when law enforcement intercepted a suspicious package sent from an invalid Colorado address to a home on Green Teal Drive in Billings. Using a warrant, investigators opened the package and discovered more than 100 grams of fentanyl in the form of 1,000 pills. A cell number associated with the package was registered to Lehman. A month later, law enforcement spoke with a source who had purchased fentanyl from a man named “Jason Holtz,” who drove a Ford F-150, and lived at the same address. By April 2025, law enforcement had learned of a second person who had purchased fentanyl from Lehman at the same address. Law enforcement then intercepted another package containing fentanyl addressed to the home. Investigators obtained a search warrant for the home and the Ford F-150, and found roughly 1,500 fentanyl pills, drug paraphernalia, a handgun, a shotgun, an assault-style rifle, and a bolt action hunting rifle. In interviews with law enforcement, Lehman acknowledged he purchased fentanyl pills online, which were shipped to his home under different names. He said he used most of the pills himself but said he also sold some and gave some away. He said he kept the guns for protection. The U.S. Attorney’s Office prosecuted the case. The United States Postal Inspection Service and Eastern Montana High Intensity Drug Trafficking Area Task Force conducted the investigation. Contact Keri Leggett Acting Public Affairs Officer keri.leggett@usdoj.gov Updated November 19, 2026 Component USAO - Montana Press Release Number: 26-307

title: Honduran national sentenced for illegally reentering the U.S.
body: Press Release Honduran national sentenced for illegally reentering the U.S. Thursday, November 19, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Montana MISSOULA – A Honduran citizen who illegally reentered the country after having previously been removed was sentenced today, U.S. Attorney Scott Twito said. U.S. District Judge William W. Mercer presided. Marcos Tulio Rodriguez-Avila, 30, who pleaded guilty in August 2026 to illegally reentering the United States, was sentenced to nine months in prison and was remanded to the custody of the U.S. Marshals Service. The government alleged in court documents that Rodriguez-Avila was arrested in March 2026 in Gallatin County on suspicion of driving under the influence. While in custody, law enforcement grew suspicious that Rodriguez-Avila may have a history of immigration arrests and removals. Officers contacted immigration officials, who confirmed Rodriguez-Avila had previously been twice removed from the U.S. for not having proper immigration documentation. The U.S. Attorney’s Office prosecuted the case. U.S. Customs and Border Protection conducted the investigation. Contact Keri Leggett Acting Public Affairs Officer keri.leggett@usdoj.gov Updated November 19, 2026 Component USAO - Montana Press Release Number: 26-308
