title: Puyallup, Washington, man sentenced to five years in prison for trafficking deadly form of fentanyl
body: Press Release Puyallup, Washington, man sentenced to five years in prison for trafficking deadly form of fentanyl Thursday, November 19, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Western District of Washington Defendant possessed more than 50,000 carfentanil pills – a drug used to sedate large animals such as elephants Tacoma – A 37-year-old Puyallup, Washington, resident was sentenced today in U.S. District Court in Tacoma to 60 months in prison for possession of controlled substances with intent to distribute, announced Acting U.S. Attorney Charles Neil Floyd. Nathaniel Washington was arrested near Centralia, Washington, on September 16, 2025. In Washington’s car were more than 50,000 pills of carfentanil – an opioid 100 times stronger than fentanyl. “Mr. Washington’s shipment was sure to bring death to drug users in western Washington. This drug is designed to sedate large animals such as elephants – putting it in a pill designed to look like oxycontin endangers addicts and casual users alike,” said Acting U.S. Attorney Floyd. “Stopping this load of drugs saved lives and has earned this defendant his federal prison time.” “Mr. Washington demonstrated a complete disregard for human life when he transported a load of deadly carfentanil pills to Western Washington for distribution,” said Robert A. Saccone, Special Agent in Charge, DEA Seattle Field Division. “Carfentanil is a synthetic opioid developed to tranquilize large animals and is estimated to be 100 times more potent than fentanyl. The potential devastation posed by more than 50,000 of these pills cannot be overstated. This seizure by DEA and our law enforcement partners prevented an enormous amount of harm. Let this sentence serve as a warning: DEA and our law enforcement partners will aggressively pursue those who traffic these deadly substances and hold them accountable.” According to records filed in the case, Washington came to the attention of law enforcement as the source of supply for a local drug trafficking ring. Law enforcement learned Washington regularly traveled to Arizona to pick up drugs, rented a car, and drove them into Western Washington for their eventual distribution on the illegal market. On September 15, law enforcement tracked Washington as he again followed this pattern – flying into Phoenix, Arizona, and beginning the drive back to Western Washington in a rental car only five hours later. This time, a DEA task force officer followed behind Washington as he pulled into a service station off I-5 heading northbound. Law enforcement detained Washington and a drug-detecting canine alerted to the car. Officers found two large vacuum-sealed bags containing 50,208 small blue pills imprinted with “M30” concealed in the lining of a suitcase in Washington’s trunk. Lab testing revealed the pills contained carfentanil, a powerful fentanyl analog used in veterinary medicine. It is 100 times stronger than fentanyl and 10,000 times stronger than morphine. DEA issued a warning when the pills were seized: when the pills were seized: Warning: Thousands of Counterfeit M30 Pills Containing Carfentanil Seized in Western Washington Nathaniel Washington was indicted by the grand jury on September 24, 2025, and pleaded guilty on July 27, 2026. In asking for a six-year sentence prosecutors wrote to the court, “The record reflects Washington has been engaging in illegal drug transactions without detection for some time. Certainly, a courier is not entrusted with the quantity of drugs Washington was caught carrying without established relationships and a proven history in the trade.” U.S. District Judge Tiffany M. Cartwright ordered Washington to be on four years of supervised release following prison. The case was jointly investigated by the Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) and the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives (ATF). The case is being prosecuted by Assistant United States Attorney Victoria Cantore. Contact Press contact for the U.S. Attorney’s Office is Communications Director Emily Langlie at (206) 553-4110 or Emily.Langlie@usdoj.gov . Updated November 19, 2026 Topics Drug Trafficking Opioids Component USAO - Washington, Western

title: Defendant Sentenced for Threatening Communications and Stalking
body: Press Release Defendant Sentenced for Threatening Communications and Stalking Thursday, November 19, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Southern District of Alabama MOBILE, ALABAMA – A Clarke County man was sentenced to 30 months in federal prison for making multiple violent and disturbing threats against a rabbi located in Alabama. According to court documents, Jeremy Wayne Shoemaker, 35, conveyed multiple violent threats, including threats of death, killing, and stalking, through voice and text communications directed at the victim.  At the time of his arrest, Shoemaker was in possession of multiple firearms and hundreds of rounds of ammunition. In addition to the 30-month term of imprisonment, Shoemaker was sentenced to three years of supervised release. “Threats motivated by hatred, intimidation, or a desire to instill fear in members of our communities will not be tolerated,” said United States Attorney Sean P. Costello.  “Religious leaders must be able to carry out their work free from threats of violence.  This sentence reflects the seriousness of the defendant’s conduct and demonstrates our unwavering commitment to protecting individuals’ civil rights and the safety of all communities across the Southern District of Alabama.” “Jeremy Shoemaker’s threats were taken seriously, and law enforcement responded with urgency,” said Christopher R. Flowers, Special Agent in Charge of the FBI Mobile Field Office.  “Within eight hours of receiving information about a potential attack, FBI Mobile and our partners executed a search warrant and took Shoemaker into custody.  Today’s sentence reflects the consequences of his actions and the importance of identifying threats before they become acts of violence.  The FBI is grateful for the critical assistance of the Clarke County Sheriff’s Office in this investigation.  We will continue working alongside our law enforcement partners to protect the public and hold those who threaten violence accountable.” The Federal Bureau of Investigations and the Clarke County Sheriff’s Office investigated the case. Assistant U.S. Attorney Gaillard Ladd prosecuted the case on behalf of the United States. A copy of this press release may be found on the website of the United States Attorney’s Office for the Southern District of Alabama at http://www.justice.gov/usao/als/ . title: Dulce Man Sentenced for Violent Assault
body: Press Release Dulce Man Sentenced for Violent Assault Thursday, November 19, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of New Mexico ALBUQUERQUE – A Dulce man was sentenced to 27 months in prison for a violent assault that left the victim with serious injuries. According to court documents, on December 31, 2025, Dennison Billy, Jr. , 36, an enrolled member of the Navajo Nation, struck an adult victim in the face with his fists while the victim was driving a vehicle in Dulce, New Mexico. Responding officers found Billy highly intoxicated in the passenger seat and the victim nearby with visible blood and multiple injuries. The victim reported exiting the vehicle to avoid further assault and was transported to a local hospital for treatment. Billy told law enforcement that he had consumed a large amount of alcohol, blacked out, and did not remember the incident. The victim sustained serious injuries, including fractures to the orbital wall and nasal bones. Billy pleaded guilty to assault resulting in serious bodily injury. There is no parole in the federal system. Upon his release from prison, Billy will be subject to three years of supervised release. First Assistant U.S. Attorney Ryan Ellison and Special Agent in Charge Justin A. Garris of the Federal Bureau of Investigation’s Albuquerque Field Office made the announcement today. The Farmington Resident Agency of the Federal Bureau of Investigation’s Albuquerque Field Office investigated this case with assistance from the Jicarilla Apache Police Department. Assistant U.S. Attorney Aaron O. Jordan is prosecuting the case. Updated November 19, 2026 Topic Indian Country Law and Justice Components Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) USAO - New Mexico Press Release Number: 26-322

title: Laramie man sentenced to 30 years in federal prison for sexual exploitation of a minor and possession of child sexual abuse material
body: Press Release Laramie man sentenced to 30 years in federal prison for sexual exploitation of a minor and possession of child sexual abuse material Thursday, November 19, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Wyoming usawy.pio@usdoj.gov CHEYENNE, Wyo. — Michael Collins Guenzel , 24, of Laramie, has been sentenced to 30 years in federal prison, followed by 10 years of supervised release, for sexual exploitation of a minor and child sexual abuse material offenses. U.S. District Court Judge Alan B. Johnson imposed the sentence. According to court documents, Guenzel was 23 years old and serving a term of felony probation in Albany County, Wyoming, when he posed online as a 16-year-old boy to target and groom a 13-year-old victim. Continuing to misrepresent his age and identity, Guenzel met the child at a hotel and sexually abused her. The crimes came to light after Guenzel’s state probation officer searched his phone and discovered sexually explicit files depicting a young girl. Upon learning of the subsequent law enforcement investigation, Guenzel texted associates and instructed them not to speak with police. On July 10, 2026, Guenzel pleaded guilty to eight federal felony counts: five counts of sexual exploitation of a minor, one count of travel with intent to engage in illicit sexual conduct with a minor, one count of receipt of child sexual abuse material and one count of possession of child sexual abuse material. “Justice cannot erase the lasting harm done to this poor girl, but today’s sentence ensures this predator is held accountable,” said U.S. Attorney Darin Smith. “This result is a testament to the unwavering dedication of the Laramie Police Department and the Wyoming Division of Criminal Investigation's Internet Crimes Against Children team.” “After the probation officer discovered concerning files on the phone, they contacted LPD and we were able to kick off this investigation, ultimately turning it over to DCI’s ICAC team for completion and leading it to a successful prosecution through the U.S. Attorney’s Office,” said Taun Smith, deputy chief of the Laramie Police Department. “This outcome is a direct result of teamwork across our criminal justice system, from the vigilance of state probation and the partnership of the Laramie Police Department to the dedicated investigators of our Internet Crimes Against Children Task Force and the prosecutor at the U.S. Attorney’s Office,” said Ryan Cox, commander of the Wyoming Division of Criminal Investigation. Assistant U.S. Attorney Mackenzie R. Morrison prosecuted the crime. This case was part of Project Safe Childhood, a nationwide Department of Justice initiative launched to combat child sexual exploitation and abuse. Project Safe Childhood marshals federal, state and local resources to locate, apprehend and prosecute individuals who exploit children via the internet, as well as to identify and rescue victims. More information is available at justice.gov/psc . ### Updated November 19, 2026 Topic Project Safe Childhood Components Criminal - Child Exploitation and Obscenity Section Defending Childhood Department of Justice USAO - Wyoming Press Release Number: 26-056

title: Previously Convicted Sex Offender Sentenced for Ninth Supervised Release Violation
body: Press Release Previously Convicted Sex Offender Sentenced for Ninth Supervised Release Violation Thursday, November 19, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of New Mexico ALBUQUERQUE – A previously convicted sex offender was sentenced to 81 months in prison for failing to update his sex offender registration and for violating the terms of his supervised release by failing to reside at a location approved by his probation officer. According to court documents, on December 29, 2025, Chebon Joe Wilson , 43, was released from prison after serving a 10-month sentence for his eighth violation of supervised release related to a 2010 conviction for abusive sexual contact. He was ordered to report to a sober living program that same day but failed to do so and did not promptly notify his probation officer of his residence. Wilson was subsequently arrested in Albuquerque on April 15, 2026, and detained. On July 29, 2026, Wilson pleaded guilty to failing to update his sex offender registration. He was sentenced to 21 months in prison for failing to register and 60 months for violating the terms of his supervised release. The sentences will run consecutively, resulting in a total prison term of 81 months. Upon his release from prison, Wilson will be subject to five years of supervised release. First Assistant U.S. Attorney Ryan Ellison and U.S. Marshal David Barnett for the District of New Mexico made the announcement today. The U.S. Marshals Service investigated this case. Assistant United States Attorney Seth Teleky prosecuted the case. Updated November 19, 2026 Topic Indian Country Law and Justice Components USAO - New Mexico U.S. Marshals Service Press Release Number: 26-323

title: Six Defendants Facing Federal Charges for their Roles in Alleged Human Trafficking Where Commercial Sex Acts Were Offered at Massage Parlors in Utah
body: Press Release Six Defendants Facing Federal Charges for their Roles in Alleged Human Trafficking Where Commercial Sex Acts Were Offered at Massage Parlors in Utah Thursday, November 19, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Utah As part of a Homeland Security Task Force led investigation, multiple defendants allegedly benefited financially from owning and operating massage parlors where a victim was coerced to engage in sexual activity SALT LAKE CITY – A federal grand jury returned an indictment charging six people – including three Chinese nationals, two of whom are illegally living in the United States – for their roles in the operation of illicit massage parlors from Orem to Ogden. As part of an undercover operation led by the Homeland Security Task Force, the alleged conduct revealed a victim was coerced into engaging in prostitution and living at a massage parlor. Yongzhen Yang, 60, a Chinese national living in Springville, Utah; Kristian Walker Bryant, 53, of Farr West, Utah; Jia Ming Zhou, 69, Chinese national living in Springville, Utah; Thomas Weyerts, 49, of Logan, Utah; and Marcus Pok Wan Chan, 38, of West Valley City, Utah, were charged by complaint on November 5. Kai Man Coco Lee, 49, of China, but previously lived in Farr West, Utah, was also indicted, along with the above defendants on November 18. According to court documents, on or about September 10, 2022, continuing through Oct. 31, in the District of Utah and elsewhere, Yang, Bryant, and Zhou enticed victim 1 to engage in a commercial sex acts, so the defendants could benefit financially. The investigation by Homeland Security Investigations revealed that Yang allegedly created and maintained several illicit massage businesses in Utah. These establishments, while operating under the guise of providing therapeutic massage services, functioned primarily as fronts for prostitution, commercial sexual exploitation, and human trafficking. As alleged, Yang would initially open various massage parlors and then sell them to others, including Bryant, and Zhou. Yang would then visit each parlor and collect proceeds from the illegal sex services provided at the parlors. As alleged in court documents, from August 15, 2019, through October 15, hundreds of advertisements were posted on websites listing various massage parlors registered by Yang, Bryant, or Zhou. These websites are known to host advertisements for sexual services and or escorts. The businesses are set for cash-only and victims have stated they only get paid if they perform sexual services. As further alleged in court documents, beginning on or about May 28, continuing through Nov. 4, Weyerts and Chan’s role in the illicit massage business was to allegedly launder money for the co-defendants. Weyerts and Chan allegedly coordinated money pickups and money deposits in various bank accounts and attempted to conceal the money by structuring deposits under $10,000.00. According to court documents, Yang is a Chinese national who overstayed on his visa in the United States and is subject of deportation proceedings. Yang has not been authorized to work in the United States since 2017. As alleged in court documents, Zhou is a Chinese national in the United States on a permanent residence card subject to expiration in 2032. She is the subject of an immigration hold resulting from this investigation. Lee, a Chinese national, and the spouse of defendant Bryant, is presently unable to return to the United States because of her lack of immigration status. All six defendants are charged with human trafficking conspiracy; sex trafficking by force, fraud, or coercion; and money laundering conspiracy. Bryant and Zhou are also charged with transporting individual to engage in prostitution. The defendants are scheduled for their initial appearances on the indictment before a U.S. Magistrate Judge at the Orrin G. Hatch United States Courthouse in downtown Salt Lake City. See docket for dates and times. United States Attorney Melissa Holyoak of the District of Utah made the announcement. The case is being investigated jointly by Homeland Security Investigations (HSI), Internal Revenue Service Criminal Investigation (IRS-CI), Murray City Police Department, and the Orem Police Department. Valuable assistance was provided by the U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE). Assistant United States Attorney Carlos A. Esqueda of the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the District of Utah is prosecuting the case. This prosecution is part of the Homeland Security Task Force (HSTF) initiative established by Executive Order 14159, Protecting the American People Against Invasion. The HSTF is a whole-of-government partnership dedicated to eliminating criminal cartels, foreign gangs, transnational criminal organizations, and human smuggling and trafficking rings operating in the United States and abroad. Through historic interagency collaboration, the HSTF directs the full might of United States law enforcement towards identifying, investigating, and prosecuting the full spectrum of crimes committed by these organizations, which have long fueled violence and instability within our borders. In performing this work, the HSTF places special emphasis on investigating and prosecuting those engaged in child trafficking or other crimes involving children. The HSTF further utilizes all available tools to prosecute and remove the most violent criminal aliens from the United States. HSTF Salt Lake comprises agents and officers from Homeland Security Investigations (HSI), Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives (ATF), Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI), and the Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) with the prosecution being led by the United States Attorney’s Office for the District of Utah. An indictment is merely an allegation and all defendants are presumed innocent until proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt in a court of law . Contact Felicia Martinez Public Affairs Specialist Felicia.martinez@usdoj.gov Updated November 19, 2026 Topic Homeland Security Task Force Component USAO - Utah Press Release Number: 26-122

title: California Man Sentenced to More Than 12 Years in Federal Prison for Trafficking Large Quantity of Cocaine
body: Press Release California Man Sentenced to More Than 12 Years in Federal Prison for Trafficking Large Quantity of Cocaine Thursday, November 19, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Eastern District of Arkansas Ms. Paulette Chappelle, Public Affairs Officer Paulette.Chappelle@usdoj.gov LITTLE ROCK—A trip from California to Memphis to deliver large amounts of narcotics ended prematurely in Arkansas for Claude Bell, who will now spend 151 months in federal prison for possession with intent to distribute five kilograms or more of cocaine. Jonathan D. Ross, United States Attorney for the Eastern District of Arkansas, announced the sentence, which was handed down today by Chief United States District Judge Kristine G. Baker. A federal grand jury indicted Bell, 58, of Lancaster, California, in a two-count Indictment for possession with intent to distribute cocaine and possession with intent to distribute fentanyl. On May 14, 2026, Bell pleaded guilty to possession with intent to distribute five kilograms or more of cocaine. Chief Judge Baker also sentenced Bell to five years’ supervised release. There is no parole in the federal system. On May 19, 2025, a trooper with the Arkansas State Police conducted a traffic stop in Russellville on a tractor-trailer being driven by Bell. During the traffic stop, the trooper observed Bell behaving nervously. Bell did not have a logbook to show his driving time and at that point, the trooper obtained consent from Bell to search the tractor and trailer. During a search of the sleeper area of the truck’s cab, the trooper located four boxes containing packages of approximately 86 pounds of cocaine and approximately 34 pounds of fentanyl. At that time, Bell was placed under arrest and agents from the Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) arrived on scene and took custody of the packaged cocaine and fentanyl. During a post- Miranda interview, Bell admitted he was paid $30,000 to transport the cocaine from Bueno Park, California, to Memphis, Tennessee. Based on a search warrant, officers reviewed Bell’s cell phone which showed he picked up the boxes in California and was traveling to deliver them to an individual at a gas station in Memphis. Bell’s prior felony convictions, which date back to 1987, include robbery, vehicle grand theft, second degree burglary of a vehicle, second-degree robbery, and second-degree attempted burglary. This case was investigated by the DEA, with assistance from the Arkansas State Police, Fifth Judicial Drug Task Force, and the Central Arkansas Drug Task Force. This case was prosecuted by Assistant United States Attorney Shelby Shelton. Updated November 19, 2026 Topic Drug Trafficking Component USAO - Arkansas, Eastern

title: Two Plead Guilty in D.C. to Trafficking Firearms from Virginia
body: Press Release Two Plead Guilty in D.C. to Trafficking Firearms from Virginia Thursday, November 19, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Columbia WASHINGTON – Moniqua Jefferson, 31 and Valentino Hall, 28, both of Richmond, Virginia, pleaded guilty today in U.S. District Court to their roles in a conspiracy that trafficked firearms from Virginia into the Washington metropolitan region, announced U.S. Attorney Jeanine Ferris Pirro. Jefferson and Hall each pleaded guilty today before Judge Ana C. Reyes to a one count of conspiracy to commit trafficking in firearms. Judge Reyes scheduled Jefferson’s sentencing for March 19, 2027, and Hall’s sentencing for April 2, 2027. A third co-defendant, Derrick Boyd, Jr., 32, of Capitol Heights, Maryland, is scheduled for trial on July 14, 2027. According to court documents, from September 2022 through September 2024, Jefferson and Hall would determine what firearms were available from federally licensed firearm retailers in the Richmond area. They then solicited interest from individuals prohibited from possessing any firearms. After determining potential buyers, Jefferson and Hall bought the guns at the licensed firearms dealers and then resold them at a markup. Jefferson and Hall purchased 24 firearms between August 2022 and May 2025. Four of those guns were recovered by law enforcement in the District of Columbia from individuals who were forbidden by law to carry or possess those firearms. Another gun, a Palmetto State Armory PA-15, allegedly was recovered in Maryland at Boyd’s residence. Boyd is a previously convicted felon and prohibited from possessing any firearm. The investigation was conducted by the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives Washington Field Division. The case is being prosecuted Special Assistant U.S. Attorney Brendan M. Horan, who is detailed to the U.S. Attorney’s Office from the United States Capitol Police, and Assistant U.S. Attorney Travis Wolf. 25cr195 Follow us on X , Instagram , and YouTube or at https://www.justice.gov/usao-dc Updated November 19, 2026 Topic Firearms Offenses Components Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives (ATF) USAO - District of Columbia

title: Brazilian National Who Allegedly Led Fake Pill Operation Charged and Extradited From Panama Following Homeland Security Task Force Investigation
body: Press Release Brazilian National Who Allegedly Led Fake Pill Operation Charged and Extradited From Panama Following Homeland Security Task Force Investigation Thursday, November 19, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Massachusetts Three co-conspirators also charged; two pill press machines, over 16 kilograms of counterfeit pills, over nine kilograms of crystal methamphetamine and five firearms seized BOSTON – A Brazilian national has been extradited from the Republic of Panama after being indicted by a federal grand jury in Boston for his alleged role in manufacturing and distributing tens of thousands of counterfeit pills containing methamphetamine. Bruno Teixeira Badaia, a/k/a “Bruno Badaya,” a/k/a “Bruno BA,” a/k/a “Bunno Sanny Silva,” 32, of Brazil, was indicted by a federal grand jury in June 2026 on one count of conspiracy to distribute and to possess with intent to distribute controlled substances (involving 50 grams or more of methamphetamine and 500 grams or more of a mixture and substance containing methamphetamine). Badaia was arrested in the Republic of Panama in September 2026 and was extradited to Massachusetts. He remains detained in federal custody following an initial appearance in federal court in Boston earlier today. Three others – Franklin Argueta, a/k/a “Frizz,” 30, of Lowell, Mass.; Luis Arias, a/k/a “Nacho,” 31, of Somerville, Mass.; and Alexis Hernandez, 27, of California – were also charged in the indictment. All four defendants were charged with conspiracy to distribute and to possess with intent to distribute controlled substances. Argueta was also charged with two counts of distribution of and possession with intent to distribute a controlled substance; one count of possession with intent to distribute controlled substances; and one count of carrying a firearm during and in relation to, and possessing a firearm in furtherance of, a drug-trafficking crime. Arias was also charged with one count of distribution of and possession with intent to distribute a controlled substance; one count of possession with intent to distribute controlled substances; and one count of possession of a firearm in furtherance of a drug-trafficking crime. According to court documents, beginning in approximately March 2025, Badaia conspired with other the defendants to manufacture and distribute methamphetamine and pills containing methamphetamine. Between August 2025 and October 2025, law enforcement conducted controlled purchases of of pills from Argueta and Arias at locations in Middlesex and Suffolk counties in Massachusetts. On Jan. 14, 2026, Argueta is alleged to have taken approximately 10,000 such pills out of his residence in Lowell and sold them to an undercover officer at a location in Middlesex County. During a search of Argueta’s residence in February 2026, it is alleged that tens of thousands of counterfeit pills suspected to contain methamphetamine, at least 9 kilograms of crystal methamphetamine and two firearms were recovered. It is further alleged that a search of Arias’s residence resulted in the recovery of tens of thousands of additional counterfeit pills suspected to contain methamphetamine and an additional firearm. Separately, two pill press machines used to manufacture counterfeit pills and dozens of bags of filler material used in the manufacturing process were also recovered. The charge of conspiracy to distribute and to possess with intent to distribute controlled substances (involving 50 grams or more of methamphetamine or 500 grams or more of a mixture and substance containing methamphetamine) provides for a sentence of no less than 10 years in prison, at least five years and up to a lifetime of supervised release and a fine of $10 million. The charges of carrying a firearm during and in relation to, and possessing a firearm in furtherance of, a drug-trafficking crime, and possession of a firearm in furtherance of a drug-trafficking crime each provide for a sentence of no less than five years and up to life in prison, to be served consecutively to the sentence for other crimes, five years of supervised release and a fine of up to $250,000. Sentences are imposed by a federal district court judge based upon the U.S. Sentencing Guidelines and statutes which govern the determination of a sentence in a criminal case. United States Attorney Leah B. Foley; Jarod A. Forget, Special Agent in Charge of the Drug Enforcement Administration, New England Field Division; Jeff Grimming, Acting Special Agent in Charge of Homeland Security Investigations in New England; and Thomas Greco, Special Agent in Charge of the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms & Explosives, Boston Field Division made the announcement. Valuable assistance was provided by Massachusetts State Police; United States Marshals Service; and the Lowell and Somerville Police Departments. The Justice Department’s Office of International Affairs worked with the Government of Panama to secure the arrest and extradition of Badaia. Assistant U.S. Attorney Samuel R. Feldman of the Narcotics & Money Laundering Unit is prosecuting the case. This case is part of the Homeland Security Task Force (HSTF) initiative established by Executive Order 14159, Protecting the American People Against Invasion. The HSTF is a whole-of-government partnership dedicated to eliminating criminal cartels, foreign gangs, transnational criminal organizations, and human smuggling and trafficking rings operating in the United States and abroad. Through historic interagency collaboration, the HSTF directs the full might of United States law enforcement towards identifying, investigating, and prosecuting the full spectrum of crimes committed by these organizations, which have long fueled violence and instability within our borders. In performing this work, the HSTF places special emphasis on investigating and prosecuting those engaged in child trafficking or other crimes involving children. The HSTF further utilizes all available tools to prosecute and remove the most violent criminal aliens from the United States. HSTF Boston is comprised of agents and officers from HSI, FBI, DEA, ATF, USMS, IRS-CI, USPIS, DOL-OIG and DSS, as well as several state and local law enforcement agencies, with the prosecution being led by the United States Attorney’s Office for the District of Massachusetts. title: New London Felon Sentenced to More Than 7 Years in Federal Prison for Firearm Offense, Violating Supervised Release
body: Press Release New London Felon Sentenced to More Than 7 Years in Federal Prison for Firearm Offense, Violating Supervised Release Thursday, November 19, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Connecticut David X. Sullivan, United States Attorney for the District of Connecticut, announced that NESTOR PAGAN, also known as Nestor Angel Vargas, 43, of New London, was sentenced today by U.S. District Judge Kari A. Dooley in Bridgeport to 90 months of imprisonment and three years of supervised release for unlawfully possessing a firearm, and for violating the conditions of his supervised release from a prior federal conviction. According to court documents and statements made in court, on April 29, 2026, U.S. Probation officers, assisted by members of the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives (ATF), the Connecticut State Police, and the New London Police Department, conducted a search of Pagan’s residence in New London and found a 9mm Smith & Wesson handgun, a .22 caliber Intratec, Tec-22 handgun, a high capacity magazine and additional gun magazines, and numerous rounds of ammunition. At the time of the search, Pagan was on federal supervised release after being convicted of unlawful possession of a firearm by a felon in 2017. Pagan’s criminal history also includes state felony convictions for first degree assault, second degree assault, sale of narcotics, and criminal weapons possession.  It is violation of federal law for a person previously convicted of a felony offense to possess a firearm or ammunition that has moved in interstate or foreign commerce. Pagan has been detained since his arrest on related state charges on April 29, 2026.  On August 27, 2026, he pleaded guilty to unlawful possession of a firearm by a felon. Judge Dooley sentenced Pagan to 78 months of imprisonment for the firearm offense, and a consecutive 12 months of imprisonment for violating the conditions of his supervised release. This matter was investigated by the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives (ATF), the Connecticut State Police, and the New London Police Department.  The case was prosecuted by Assistant U.S. Attorneys Justyn P. Stokely and Jocelyn Courtney Kaoutzanis. This case is part of Operation Take Back America, a nationwide initiative that marshals the full resources of the Department of Justice to repel the invasion of illegal immigration, achieve the total elimination of cartels and transnational criminal organizations (TCOs), and protect our communities from the perpetrators of violent crime. title: Northeast Georgia Man Charged with International Money Laundering and  Destroying Evidence Tied to ISIS
body: Press Release Northeast Georgia Man Charged with International Money Laundering and  Destroying Evidence Tied to ISIS Thursday, November 19, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release Office of Public Affairs Northeast Georgia Man Charged with International Money Laundering and  Destroying Evidence Tied to ISIS Note : Please see the complaint here . A Lavonia, Georgia, resident is in federal custody charged by criminal complaint with international money laundering and destruction of evidence following an FBI investigation into allegations of sending more than $26,000 to individuals and groups affiliated with a designated foreign terrorist organization, the Islamic State of Iraq and al Sham (ISIS). Younes Moustafa Younes, 34, of Lavonia, Georgia, was charged by complaint with one count of international money laundering and one count of destruction of evidence. If convicted, Younes faces a maximum penalty of 20 years in prison, to be followed by three years of supervised release, and a $500,000 fine for international money laundering, and a maximum penalty of 20 years in prison, to be followed by three years of supervised release, and a $250,000 fine for destroying evidence. He made his initial appearance today in federal court before U.S. Magistrate Judge Charles Weigle and will remain in federal custody pending his preliminary and detention hearings on Nov. 23 in Macon. Alleged images of Younes on March 10, 2022 (top) and on May 6, 2026 (bottom) were captured by cryptocurrency ATMs According to the complaint, between December 2025 and June 2026, Younes sent $16,807 through cryptocurrency transactions using multiple phone numbers and accounts intended to conceal his identity. Investigators allege that at least some of the funds were intended to promote the efforts of ISIS in Syria. In addition, Younes is alleged to have altered and destroyed evidence up until his arrest on Nov. 18, when FBI Atlanta agents executed warrants to search his apartment, car, electronic devices, and workplace. The FBI found three cellular phones submerged in an unknown solution inside his Lavonia apartment, including one device that was smashed and another with its identification number removed. Agents also found shredded documents submerged in an unknown solution in a bathtub. Destroyed cell phones (top) in an unknown liquid solution and shredded paper (bottom) in an unknown liquid solution found in Younes’ Lavonia, Georgia, apartment on Nov. 18, 2026. The FBI first identified Younes in 2020 after he allegedly accessed ISIS propaganda online. When interviewed by law enforcement, Younes acknowledged viewing the material but denied supporting extremist ideologies. The complaint alleges that, over time, Younes became increasingly radicalized, expressing support for ISIS and other terrorist figures and organizations through encrypted communications with associates. The complaint further alleges that in 11 separate transactions between December 2021 and April 2022, Younes is alleged to have sent approximately $9,206 to cryptocurrency addresses associated with this effort, using an alias to conceal his support. Encrypted communications cited in the complaint allegedly show Younes sharing extremist content, discussing support for ISIS, and praising individuals associated with terrorist organizations. In September 2022, Younes traveled to Turkey on a one-way ticket and remained there for approximately two years after allegedly selling his vehicle, cashing out retirement funds, and leaving his employment in the United States. Following his arrest and deportation from Turkey back to the United States, investigators allege that Younes continued to express support for extremist causes and maintained contacts with individuals previously convicted on terrorism-related charges. FBI Atlanta is investigating the case, with assistance from FBI Newark and the National Counterterrorism Center. Criminal Chief Leah McEwen and Assistant U.S. Attorney Daniel Peach for the Middle District of Georgia, Assistant U.S. Attorney Sammi Malek for the District of New Jersey, and the National Security Division's Counterterrorism Section are prosecuting the case for the government. A criminal complaint is merely allegations of criminal conduct. All defendants are presumed innocent until proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt in a court of law. title: Former Hacienda Employee Sentenced to 50 Months in Prison for His Participation in a Bribery Conspiracy Involving Loss of $5 Million
body: Press Release Former Hacienda Employee Sentenced to 50 Months in Prison for His Participation in a Bribery Conspiracy Involving Loss of $5 Million Thursday, November 19, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Puerto Rico SAN JUAN, Puerto Rico – On November 18, 2026, United States District Court Judge Silvia Carreño Coll sentenced former Hacienda employee Luis A. Jiménez-Guzmán to 50 months in prison, two years of supervised release, and restitution of 5 million dollars for his role in a bribery conspiracy to defraud the Puerto Rico Department of Treasury (PRDT or Hacienda), announced Héctor Ramírez Carbó, Acting United States Attorney for the District of Puerto Rico.  On July 2, 2026, Jiménez-Guzmán was charged and pleaded guilty to a bribery conspiracy involving the loss of approximately $5,000,000 in Puerto Rico tax revenue, in violation of 18 U.S.C. § 371. According to the plea agreement in the case, Luis A. Jiménez-Guzmán, knowingly and willfully conspired to commit federal program bribery and wire fraud, as well as accepted bribe payments in exchange for his corrupt acts. From February 2019 through March 2023, Jiménez-Guzmán was an employee and agent of the PRDT with duties that included physically and electronically accessing and reviewing tax returns and documents related to invoicing and collection of owed taxes. The defendant had privileged access to the PRDT’s online platforms, the Puerto Rico Integrated Tax Administration System (PRITAS) and the Internal Revenue Unified System (GenTax/SURI) and was able to access, monitor, and modify taxpayer information, including creating taxpayer credits, modifying income tax, employee retention tax and sales tax information. As part of the bribery conspiracy, Jiménez-Guzmán corruptly accepted cash payments and other benefits, in exchange for submitting false information to the PRDT. The false information was submitted to the PRDT for the elimination of taxes owed, evasion of taxes, and theft of funds. For example, on August 16, 2021, Jiménez-Guzmán received a $10,000 bribe payment from Person H to erase and reduce a tax debt of one of Person H’s customers. The illicit payments were solicited and accepted by Jiménez-Guzmán, who illegally eliminated the PRDT tax liabilities and obtained illegal tax refunds for several individual and business taxpayers, with a total approximate loss to the PRDT of $5,000,000. Acting U.S. Attorney Héctor Ramírez-Carbó of the District of Puerto Rico; and Carlos R. Goris, Special Agent in Charge of FBI San Juan Field Office made the announcement. The Federal Bureau of Investigation investigated these matters. Assistant U.S. Attorney Marie Christine Amy from the District of Puerto Rico’s Financial Fraud & Public Corruption Section prosecuted this case. This is part of an ongoing effort to combat public corruption and fraud committed by Puerto Rico Department of Treasury employees. The U.S. Attorney’s Office for the District of Puerto Rico previously announced the indictment of twenty-six individuals and corporations in October 2025 and the guilty pleas of three Hacienda employees, Luis A. Jiménez-Guzmán , Harry E. Mueriel-Falero , and Alexander Ortiz-Robles . # # # Updated November 19, 2026 Topics Fraud Financial Fraud Public Corruption Components Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) USAO - Puerto Rico Press Release Number: 2026-126

title: Federal Jury Convicts Fifth Defendant for Scheme to Assassinate Haitian President Jovenel Moïse in Homeland Security Task Force Investigation
body: Press Release Federal Jury Convicts Fifth Defendant for Scheme to Assassinate Haitian President Jovenel Moïse in Homeland Security Task Force Investigation Thursday, November 19, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Southern District of Florida MIAMI – A federal jury in Miami convicted a fifth defendant for his role in the July 7, 2021, assassination of Haitian President Jovenel Moïse. Christian Emmanuel Sanon, 67, was convicted of conspiracy to provide material support or resources to carry out a violation of 18 U.S.C. § 956, resulting in death; providing material support and resources to carry out a violation of 18 U.S.C. § 956, resulting in death; conspiracy to kill and kidnap a person outside the United States; two counts of conspiracy to commit offenses against the United States; expedition against a friendly nation; smuggling goods from the United States; and submitting false or misleading export information. He faces a maximum penalty of life in federal prison. A federal district court judge will determine any sentence after considering the U.S. Sentencing Guidelines and other statutory factors. “Sanon helped orchestrate one of the most brazen acts of political violence in the Western Hemisphere in recent history,” said Acting Principal Deputy Assistant Attorney General for National Security M. Scott Proctor. “The brutal murder of President Jovenel Moïse in his own home was a direct assault on Haiti’s government and a devastating crime against the Haitian people. This conviction ensures that another participant in this conspiracy is held accountable and reaffirms that the United States will not tolerate its territory or financial systems being used to facilitate acts of terror abroad.” “The assassination of a sitting president is an attack not only on a life, but on the sovereignty of a nation and the very foundations of democracy,” said Acting U.S. Attorney Yara Lorenzo Klukas for the Southern District of Florida. “President Moïse was brutally murdered in his own home, his wife was gravely wounded, and a nation was left to confront the devastating consequences of political violence. Yesterday, a jury of his peers held this defendant accountable for his role in that horrific crime. This verdict sends an unmistakable message: those who seek power through violence and political assassination will find no safe haven in the United States. We remain steadfast in our pursuit of justice for President Moïse, his family, and the people of Haiti, and I am deeply grateful to the prosecutors, investigators, and law enforcement partners whose tireless work made this verdict possible.” “This guilty verdict against Christian Sanon marks another significant step toward accountability in the assassination of Haitian President Jovenel Moïse,” said Special Agent in Charge Brett D. Skiles of the FBI Miami Field Office. “The FBI remains committed to pursuing justice and holding those responsible accountable. No matter how long it takes or where you hide, justice will find you.” “Christian Sanon’s guilty verdict reflects the gravity of his role in a conspiracy that culminated in the assassination of Haitian President Jovenel Moïse,” said Special Agent in Charge Jose R. Figueroa of Homeland Security Investigations (HSI) Miami. “This is a strong reminder that those who plan, finance, enable or support transnational violence will be held accountable under U.S. law. HSI, alongside our domestic and international law enforcement partners, remains committed to pursuing every individual responsible for this criminal plot and ensuring justice is served.” According to court records and evidence presented at trial, Sanon kickstarted a conspiracy in early 2021 to violently overthrow President Moïse and install himself as Haiti’s next president. Working with co-conspirators Arcangel Pretel Ortiz, Antonio Intriago, Walter Veintemilla, James Solages, and others in the United States and Haiti, Sanon promised lucrative future government infrastructure contracts in exchange for their financial, logistical, and operational support in kidnapping or killing President Moïse. Throughout the conspiracy, Sanon falsely claimed to have the backing of the U.S. Department of State to recruit allies and garner support for the plot. He often used American flags and other government imagery to lend credibility to his false claims. When the plan to emplace Sanon as the new president stalled, he agreed to assume a secondary role in the conspirators’ planned new Haitian government and remained firmly involved in the conspiracy, arranging transportation, lodging, food, equipment, and other supplies for the 22 Colombian mercenaries who assassinated President Moïse. In mid-June 2021, Sanon helped smuggle ballistic vests from the United States into Haiti for the Colombian mercenaries. In late June 2021, Sanon also sent Solages – Sanon’s right-hand man – back to the United States to obtain additional tactical and operational advice and finalize plans for the assassination. On July 7, 2021, Solages and a team of Colombian mercenaries, aided by several Haitian allies, carried out the attack on President Moïse’s residence. During the assault, a squad of former Colombian special forces soldiers known as the Delta Team, along with other mercenaries, stormed the residence and fatally shot President Moïse in his bedroom. The attackers also seriously wounded Haiti’s First Lady, Martine Moïse. Digital evidence presented at trial revealed months of extensive communications between Sanon and his co-conspirators detailing their plans to kidnap or kill President Moïse. The evidence also showed that, shortly before his arrest on July 9, 2021, Sanon deleted most of the incriminating communications from his three cellphones, including communications in which Sanon discussed what he expected to gain from the plot immediately after the assassination. Eight co-conspirators, including two Colombian mercenaries and several Haitian and American associates, have pleaded guilty to their roles in the conspiracy. In May, a federal jury convicted Pretel Ortiz, Intriago, Veintemilla, and Solages. In September, 29 additional defendants were indicted for their alleged roles in the plot to assassinate President Moïse. The charges include an intertwined fraud and money laundering scheme involving funds obtained through the Paycheck Protection Program (PPP), a federal COVID-19 relief program, that allegedly helped finance the assassination plot. Assistant U.S. Attorneys Sean T. McLaughlin, Jason Wu, and Altanese Phenelus for the Southern District of Florida are prosecuting the case. This prosecution is part of the Homeland Security Task Force (HSTF) initiative established by Executive Order 14159, Protecting the American People Against Invasion. The HSTF is a whole-of-government partnership dedicated to eliminating criminal cartels, foreign gangs, transnational criminal organizations, and human smuggling and trafficking rings operating in the United States and abroad. Through historic interagency collaboration, the HSTF directs the full might of United States law enforcement towards identifying, investigating, and prosecuting the full spectrum of crimes committed by these organizations, which have long fueled violence and instability within our borders. In performing this work, the HSTF places special emphasis on investigating and prosecuting those engaged in child trafficking or other crimes involving children. The HSTF further utilizes all available tools to prosecute and remove the most violent criminal aliens from the United States. HSTF Miami comprises agents and officers from Homeland Security Investigations; FBI; Drug Enforcement Administration; Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives; U.S. Department of State’s Diplomatic Security Service; IRS Criminal Investigation; U.S. Marshals Service; U.S. Postal Inspection Service; U.S. Secret Service; U.S. Coast Guard; U.S. Coast Guard Investigative Services; U.S. Customs and Border Protection’s Office of Field Operations; U.S. Border Patrol; U.S. Customs and Border Protection’s Air and Marine Operations; ICE’s Enforcement and Removal Operations; South Florida High Intensity Drug Trafficking Area, and state, local, and tribal law enforcement agencies with the prosecution being led by the United States Attorney’s Office for the Southern District of Florida. Related court documents and information may be found on the website of the District Court for the Southern District of Florida at www.flsd.uscourts.gov or at http://pacer.flsd.uscourts.gov , under case number 22-cr-20104. ### Contact Public Affairs Unit U.S. Attorney’s Office Southern District of Florida USAFLS.News@usdoj.gov Updated November 19, 2026 Topic National Security Component USAO - Florida, Southern

title: Justice Department’s Statement on the Closing of Its Investigation of NextEra’s Acquisition of Dominion
body: Press Release Justice Department’s Statement on the Closing of Its Investigation of NextEra’s Acquisition of Dominion Thursday, November 19, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release Office of Public Affairs The U.S. Department of Justice issued the following statement today in connection with the closing of the Antitrust Division’s investigation into the acquisition of Dominion Energy Inc. (Dominion) by NextEra Energy Inc. (NextEra) (together, “the Parties”): The Antitrust Division continues to focus on the needs of electricity customers across the country to ensure that they benefit from competition among electricity generators. As demands on electricity grids increase, it is critical that wholesale electricity and capacity markets are competitive and cannot be exploited in a way that could leave American businesses and consumers facing higher electricity bills. The Parties’ commitment to FERC eliminating their unilateral right to deactivate units in New England will protect consumers in the region from potentially hundreds of millions of dollars of increased electricity costs. On May 18, NextEra and Dominion announced an agreement to combine the two companies in a $66.8 billion transaction. Both firms are electricity generation companies that compete in wholesale electricity and electric capacity auctions run by Regional Transmission Organizations (RTOs) or Independent System Operators (ISOs). RTOs and ISOs are nonprofit organizations responsible for managing and operating electric power grids within specific regions of the United States. These organizations rely on internal or external market monitors, who are responsible for overseeing and evaluating the electricity market’s performance. NextEra’s acquisition of Dominion combines overlapping electricity generation asset portfolios in two separate RTO/ISOs: PJM Interconnection LLC (which covers portions of the Midwest and Mid-Atlantic) and ISO New England Inc. (ISO-NE). As required by federal law, NextEra and Dominion have filed an application with the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) for approval of the transaction. During FERC’s ongoing review process, the Internal Market Monitor of ISO-NE submitted comments to FERC regarding the potential impact of the transaction on the electric capacity market. Electric capacity markets ensure the availability of a reserve of capacity that an ISO or RTO can call on to provide network reliability during periods of peak electricity demand. They do this by paying generators to keep plants on-call and available to produce electricity, independent of any payments the generators receive from the sale of electricity generation. The Internal Market Monitor expressed concerns that the transaction might give the merged firm the incentive and ability to deactivate a plant that still is economically viable with the goal of using its combined portfolio to increase capacity payments in New England. To address this concern, the Internal Market Monitor proposed that the merged firm agree to allow the Internal Market Monitor to investigate any plant that the merged firm proposes to deactivate for a five-year period beginning with the next ISO-NE capacity auction in May 2028. If the Internal Market Monitor determines that the plant continues to have economic value, then NextEra would be prohibited from deactivating it. Following a detailed investigation — which included review of documents, interviews of industry participants, and sophisticated economic modeling — the Division remained concerned about the potential impact of the transaction on ISO-NE’s capacity market. After the Division informed the Parties of these concerns, the Parties told FERC in a filing on FERC’s docket that they will “commit, without qualification , to comply” with the Internal Market Monitor’s proposal regardless of whether FERC imposes it as a condition for approval of the transaction. In light of the Division’s review and the Parties’ commitment to FERC, the Antitrust Division decided that its investigation could be closed. title: Massachusetts Maritime Academy Assistant Football Coach Arrested for Allegedly Sexually Exploiting Minors
body: Press Release Massachusetts Maritime Academy Assistant Football Coach Arrested for Allegedly Sexually Exploiting Minors Thursday, November 19, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Massachusetts Defendant allegedly posed as a teenager online and solicited child sexual abuse material from at least five minors BOSTON – An assistant football coach at Massachusetts Maritime Academy was arrested today and charged with allegedly possessing child sexual abuse material (CSAM) and inducing an 11-year-old girl to produce CSAM. Garrett Luke Owens, 28, of Buzzards Bay, Mass., was charged by criminal complaint with one count of sexual exploitation of children and one count of possession of child pornography. Owens was arrested this morning and remains detained following an initial appearance today in federal court in Boston. According to the charging documents, during the investigation it was determined that Owens allegedly communicated with at least five minor victims through text messaging and social-media applications, including Snapchat and TikTok. Owens allegedly used aliases including “Garry,” “Garrison,” and “Grayson,” falsely representing himself to be a 15- or 16-year-old boy and soliciting sexually explicit images and videos from underage girls. It is alleged that the investigation began after law enforcement in Crete, Neb., reviewed the phone of a 14-year-old girl and discovered sexually explicit communications with a contact named “Garry.” The telephone number associated with the communications was allegedly linked to Owens. Records associated with Owens’ iCloud account allegedly contained child sexual abuse material involving multiple minor victims. According to the complaint, additional victims were identified in Texas, New Mexico and Maine. The victims allegedly reported that Owens initially contacted them through TikTok or other social-media platforms before moving the communications to Snapchat or text messaging. Owens allegedly continued to solicit sexually explicit material after learning that the victims were minors and, in some instances, after the victims specifically disclosed their ages. A preliminary review of Owens’ cellphone allegedly revealed sexually explicit videos involving minors stored in a hidden photo folder. Investigators also allegedly found communications with an 11-year-old girl in which Owens confirmed her age and then induced her, through an online game, to remove her clothing and expose herself on video. The charge of sexual exploitation of children provides for a mandatory minimum sentence of 15 years and up to 30 years in prison, at least five years and up to a lifetime of supervised release and a fine of up to $250,000. The charge of possession of child pornography provides for a sentence of up to 20 years in prison, at least five years and up to a lifetime of supervised release and a fine of up to $250,000. Sentences are imposed by a federal district court judge based upon the U.S. Sentencing Guidelines and statutes governing the determination of a sentence in a criminal case. United States Attorney Leah B. Foley and Jeff Grimming, Acting Special Agent in Charge of Homeland Security Investigations in New England made the announcement today. Valuable assistance was provided by the Crete (Neb.) Police Department; HSI Houston; HSI Roswell; HSI Bangor; and other federal, state and local law enforcement partners. Assistant U.S. Attorney Luke A. Goldworm, of the Major Crimes Unit and Project Safe Childhood Coordinator and Assistant U.S. Attorney Catherine Conroy of the Major Crimes Unit are prosecuting the case. This case is brought as part of Project Safe Childhood. In 2006, the Department of Justice created Project Safe Childhood, a nationwide initiative designed to protect children from exploitation and abuse. Led by the U.S. Attorneys’ Offices and the Department’s Child Exploitation and Obscenity Section, Project Safe Childhood marshals federal, state and local resources to locate, apprehend and prosecute individuals who exploit children, as well as identify and rescue victims. For more information about Project Safe Childhood, please visit www.justice.gov/psc . The details contained in the charging document are allegations. The defendant is presumed to be innocent unless and until proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt in the court of law. title: New York City Man Pleads Guilty to Sending a White Powder Letter to the Superintendent of the Coxsackie Correctional Facility
body: Press Release New York City Man Pleads Guilty to Sending a White Powder Letter to the Superintendent of the Coxsackie Correctional Facility Thursday, November 19, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Northern District of New York USANYN-MediaInquiry@usa.doj.gov On November 12, 2026, James McDonaugh, age 49, of Manhattan, New York, pled guilty to conveying a hoax involving a white powder letter.  First Assistant United States Attorney John A. Sarcone III and Craig L. Tremaroli, Special Agent in Charge of the Albany Field Office for the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI), made the announcement. As part of his guilty plea, McDonaugh admitted that on December 17, 2024, while serving as an inmate at the Coxsackie Correctional Facility, he used the prison’s internal mail system to send an envelope to the prison’s Superintendent.  The envelope contained a letter and some white powder.  The letter said “ANtrax DIE BITCH”. McDonaugh further admitted that he intended to scare members of the Superintendent’s staff into believing that anthrax, a dangerous biological agent, was in the envelope. McDonaugh faces up to five years of imprisonment, a $250,000 fine, and up to three years of supervised release. A defendant’s sentence is imposed by a judge based on the particular statute(s) the defendant is convicted of violating, the U.S. Sentencing Guidelines and other factors. Sentencing is currently scheduled for March 15, 2027, at 12:30 pm in Albany, New York, before U.S. District Judge, Elizabeth C. Coombe. First Assistant United States Attorney John A. Sarcone III said: “Using white powder letter hoaxes to scare members of law enforcement who are simply doing their job will not be tolerated by my office. Mr. McDonaugh’s actions have earned him some additional time behind bars.” “Mr. McDonaugh’s reckless decision to send a hoax white powder letter through the prison’s mail system just extended his stay behind bars,” said Craig Tremaroli, Special Agent in Charge of the Federal Bureau of Investigation’s Albany Field Office. “The FBI takes hoax threats very seriously and will continue to work with our law enforcement partners to ensure anyone who tries to cause fear and chaos through these calculated actions is brought to justice. The FBI investigated the case with assistance from the New York State Department of Corrections and Community Supervision.  Assistant U.S. Attorney Rick Belliss is prosecuting the case. Updated November 19, 2026 Topic Domestic Terrorism Component USAO - New York, Northern

title: DeMotte Man Sentenced to 204 Months in Prison for Child Pornography Offenses
body: Press Release DeMotte Man Sentenced to 204 Months in Prison for Child Pornography Offenses Thursday, November 19, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Northern District of Indiana HAMMOND – Linden Urbano, 29 years old, of DeMotte, Indiana, was sentenced by United States District Court Judge Philip P. Simon after pleading guilty to multiple offenses involving the production and receipt of child pornography, announced United States Attorney Adam L. Mildred. Urbano was sentenced to 204 months in prison and 10 years of supervised release.  He was also ordered to pay a $5,000 assessment pursuant to the Amy, Vicky, and Andy Child Pornography Victim Assistance Act of 2018, which will be deposited into the Child Pornography Victims Reserve and made available to victims of trafficking of child pornography. According to documents in the case, Urbano utilized dating and social networking applications to meet and communicate with his victims, all of whom were under the age of 18. Urbano instructed some of his victims to send him sexually explicit material depicting themselves, and he provided directions to those victims on how to pose for the camera. He also persuaded and enticed some of his victims to meet him in-person for sex and then produced videos of himself sexually exploiting them. He sent at least one of the videos he produced to an associate in another state. “Linden Urbano will spend the next 17 years in prison for sexually exploiting five minors he met online. These offenses have life-altering, lasting impacts on victims and their families and require punishment which reflects the seriousness of the crimes and which will deter others from engaging in this heinous behavior. I am thankful for the victims and their parents who came forward, despite difficult circumstances, to ensure that Mr. Urbano was held accountable for his actions. The United States Attorney’s Office will use all resources at our disposal to aggressively prosecute these offenders and obtain justice for their victims,” said U.S. Attorney Mildred. This case was investigated by the Federal Bureau of Investigation with valuable assistance provided by the Indiana State Police, the Jasper County Sheriff’s Office, the Oakland County (Michigan) Sheriff’s Office, and the DeMotte Police Department. The case was prosecuted by Assistant United States Attorney Steven J. Lupa. This case was brought as part of Project Safe Childhood, a nationwide initiative to combat the growing epidemic of child sexual exploitation and abuse launched in May 2006 by the Department of Justice. Led by U.S. Attorneys' Offices and CEOS, Project Safe Childhood marshals federal, state, and local resources to better locate, apprehend and prosecute individuals who exploit children via the Internet, as well as to identify and rescue victims. For more information about Project Safe Childhood, please visit Justice.gov/PSC . ### Updated November 19, 2026 Topic Project Safe Childhood Components Science and Technology Branch (FBI) USAO - Indiana, Northern

title: Federal grand jury indicts five alleged members of North Texas drug trafficking organization
body: Press Release Federal grand jury indicts five alleged members of North Texas drug trafficking organization Thursday, November 19, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Northern District of Texas DALLAS — United States Attorney for the Northern District of Texas Ryan Raybould announced that a federal grand jury has returned an indictment charging five individuals for their alleged roles in a drug trafficking conspiracy involving methamphetamine, heroin, and fentanyl in the Dallas area. Jose Mendoza, Roberto Duran, Kamerun Francis Herlehy, Julie Lynn Wilson, and Brooke Harrell are charged with conspiracy to possess with intent to distribute controlled substances. The indictment alleges that from approximately July through the beginning of October, the defendants conspired to distribute more than 500 grams of methamphetamine, more than one kilogram of heroin, and fentanyl. In addition to the conspiracy charge, Jose Mendoza is charged with possession with intent to distribute 500 grams or more of methamphetamine and possession of a firearm in furtherance of a drug trafficking crime. The indictment alleges that Mendoza possessed a Ruger LCP semi-automatic handgun in furtherance of his drug trafficking activities on or about October 1. Kamerun Francis Herlehy is also charged with possession of a firearm in furtherance of a drug trafficking crime. According to the indictment, Herlehy possessed a Sig Sauer P938 pistol in furtherance of the charged drug trafficking conspiracy on or about August 20. “The distribution of methamphetamine, heroin, and fentanyl threatens the safety and well-being of our communities,” said U.S. Attorney Ryan Raybould. “This case represents the successful dismantling of a large-scale drug trafficking organization responsible for flooding Dallas-area streets with deadly narcotics. Through the coordinated efforts of our federal, state, and local law enforcement partners, we disrupted a network that profited from addiction and fueled violence throughout our communities. We will continue to aggressively pursue those who traffic these dangerous substances and hold them accountable.” “This investigation targeted a criminal organization that was trafficking large quantities of methamphetamine, heroin and fentanyl, all while using firearms in furtherance of this criminal operation,” said DEA Dallas Field Division Special Agent in Charge Joseph B. Tucker. “We will continue to work with our federal, state, and local partners, to identify, disrupt, and dismantle these networks to protect our communities and hold accountable those who prioritize profit over law.” The indictment includes forfeiture allegations seeking approximately $59,033 in U.S. currency and multiple firearms allegedly used in connection with the charged offenses, including the Ruger and Sig Sauer pistols identified in the indictment. If convicted, Mendoza, Duran, and Herlehy face substantial prison terms . The drug conspiracy charge carries a mandatory minimum sentence of 10 years in federal prison and a maximum sentence of life imprisonment, with enhanced penalties potentially applicable to certain defendants based on prior felony drug convictions. The firearm charges carry mandatory consecutive prison sentences. The Drug Enforcement Administration Dallas Division, Texas Department of Public Safety, and the Dallas Police Department conducted the investigation. Assistant U.S. Attorney Abby Policastro from the Cartel and National Security Section is prosecuting the case. An indictment is merely an allegation. All defendants are presumed innocent until proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt in a court of law. Contact Public Affairs Division U.S. Attorney’s Office Northern District of Texas USATXN.Media@usdoj.gov Updated November 19, 2026 Topic Drug Trafficking Component USAO - Texas, Northern

title: Waterbury Man Admits Role in Mail Theft Scheme
body: Press Release Waterbury Man Admits Role in Mail Theft Scheme Thursday, November 19, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Connecticut David X. Sullivan, United States Attorney for the District of Connecticut, and Justin Page, Acting Inspector in Charge of the U.S. Postal Inspection Service, Boston Division, announced that MARCUS ANTHONY SIMMS, 28, of Waterbury, waived his right to be indicted and pleaded guilty today before U.S. District Judge Omar A. Williams in Hartford to conspiracy to steal U.S. mail. According to court documents and statements made in court, early in the morning on May 26, 2025, Simms drove with two associates to the Milford Post Office on Pepes Farm Road in Milford.  While Simms remained inside the vehicle, his associates exited the vehicle and attempted to pry open a large U.S. Postal Service collection box using a screwdriver and other tools.  The co-conspirators damaged the collection box, particularly the locking mechanism, but were unable to open it.  The screwdriver was left at the scene. Simms was arrested on November 7, 2025. At sentencing, which is not scheduled, Simms faces a maximum term of imprisonment of five years.  He also has agreed to pay $4,139 in restitution to the USPS. Simms is released on a $100,000 bond pending sentencing, This matter has been investigated by the U.S. Postal Inspection Service and the Milford Police Department.  The case is being prosecuted by Assistant U.S. Attorney Hal Chen. Updated November 19, 2026 Component USAO - Connecticut

title: Two Illegal Aliens Plead Guilty to Smuggling Illegal Aliens Into the United States
body: Press Release Two Illegal Aliens Plead Guilty to Smuggling Illegal Aliens Into the United States Thursday, November 19, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Nevada RENO – A father and son, both illegal aliens from Mexico, each pleaded guilty to their roles in a human smuggling operation that brought in and harbored illegal aliens in the Reno area for financial gain. “These defendants prioritized illicit profit over human life and the rule of law, operating a family-run smuggling enterprise that endangered both the individuals they transported and the communities along our border,” said First Assistant United States Attorney Sigal Chattah for the District of Nevada. “Working alongside our federal and local law enforcement partners, our office remains committed to dismantling human smuggling networks at every level and holding those who exploit our nation’s immigration laws fully accountable.” “Human smugglers who exploit vulnerable people through coercion, threats and demands for payment will be pursued and held accountable,” said Jonathan Sherwin, Deputy Special Agent in Charge for HSI Las Vegas. “HSI and our law enforcement partners will continue to dismantle the networks that profit from smuggling and harboring illegal aliens, while protecting those subjected to exploitation and abuse.” According to court documents and statements made in court, from November 1, 2024, and continuing up to March 11, 2025, Carlos Recinos-Valdez aided another person with bringing more than six but less than 25 illegal aliens into the United States. The illegal aliens were detained through coercion or threat or in connection with a demand for payment after the alien was smuggled into the United States or while the alien was transported or harbored in the United States. On March 13, 2023, and continuing up to March 11, 2025, Recinos-Valdez’s son Kevin Recinos-Ruano conspired with others to harbor illegal aliens in buildings in and around Reno and transporting illegal aliens between the buildings. The buildings where the illegal aliens were harbored were controlled and paid for by other members of the conspiracy to hide the aliens from law enforcement. Recinos-Ruano pleaded guilty today to one count of conspiracy to harbor illegal aliens. He faces a maximum statutory penalty of five years in prison. Sentencing is scheduled for December 2, 2026. Recinos-Valdez pleaded guilty on November 17, 2026, to one count of aiding and abetting bringing illegal aliens into the United States. He faces a maximum statutory penalty of 10 years in prison with a minimum statutory penalty of three years in prison. Sentencing is scheduled for February 16, 2027. HSI investigated the case with significant assistance from the Reno Police Department, the Sparks Police Department, the Douglas County Sheriff’s Office, and the Washoe County Sheriff’s Office. Assistant United States Attorney Clay Plummer is prosecuting the case. You can report suspicious criminal activity to the ICE Tip Line 24 hours a day, seven days a week by calling 866-DHS-2-ICE (866-347-2423) or online at https://www.ice.gov/webform/ice-tip-form . ### Updated November 19, 2026 Topic Human Smuggling Component USAO - Nevada

body: Press Release Detroit Man Sentenced to 5 Years in Prison for Five-Year Identity Theft Scheme Thursday, November 19, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Eastern District of Michigan DETROIT – Terrence Quincy-Thomas Ward, 34, of Detroit, was sentenced today to 5 years in federal prison for operating a five-year identity theft and credit card fraud scheme that caused more than $200,000 in losses, announced U.S. Attorney Jerome F. Gorgon, Jr. Ward previously pleaded guilty to wire fraud and aggravated identity theft. From 2020 through 2025, Ward illicitly obtained victims’ personal identifying information, manufactured fake driver’s licenses, and used that information to open fraudulent credit card accounts. When agents executed a search warrant at Ward's residence, they recovered counterfeit Social Security cards, fraudulent driver's licenses, and equipment used to manufacture fake identification documents: In total, 205 credit card accounts were compromised, resulting in losses of approximately $200,696.84. This case was investigated by the U.S. Department of Labor, Office of Inspector General, and the Department of Homeland Security Investigations. title: Convicted Murderer Sentenced to More Than 20 Years for Armed Carjacking and Witness Tampering
body: Press Release Convicted Murderer Sentenced to More Than 20 Years for Armed Carjacking and Witness Tampering Thursday, November 19, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Northern District of Oklahoma TULSA, Okla. – U.S. District Judge Sara E. Hill sentenced Christopher Ray Barrett, 41, to 246 months in federal prison for carjacking, brandishing a firearm during a crime of violence, possessing a firearm and ammunition as a convicted felon, and conspiring to tamper with witnesses. Barrett pleaded guilty to the charges in November 2025. According to court documents, Barrett, who goes by the alias “SloMo,” forcibly took a victim’s 2012 Volkswagen Passat at gunpoint on Dec. 29, 2024. After the victim drove an acquaintance to a Tulsa residence, Barrett entered the vehicle, pressed a revolver against the victim’s head, and demanded information about property inside the car. Barrett then forced the victim to unload the vehicle, confiscated the victim’s keys and cellphone, and threatened multiple individuals at the residence with the revolver. Court records show Barrett held the victim at gunpoint inside the residence for approximately one hour, before forcibly abducting the victim to retrieve the Passat’s title from the victim’s home. Days later, Tulsa Police officers located Barrett driving the stolen Passat and recovered a loaded Smith & Wesson .38-caliber revolver from inside the vehicle. Law enforcement’s continued investigation revealed that, following his arrest, Barrett conspired with others to locate and threaten  witnesses to the carjacking in an effort to prevent their testimony in the federal case. Barrett directed the witness tampering conspiracy while incarcerated pending trial. According to sentencing records, Barrett committed these offenses only months after being released from a twenty-year state prison sentence. Additionally, Oklahoma state courts had previously imposed six lifetime suspended sentences. Barrett’s criminal history includes convictions for second-degree murder, assault with a dangerous weapon, felon in possession of a firearm, and multiple vehicle theft-related crimes. The Court found that Barrett’s extensive history of violent criminal  and continued criminal conduct warranted a substantial federal sentence. Two additional defendants were prosecuted for their participation in the witness-tampering conspiracy and have also been sentenced. The Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms, and Explosives and the Tulsa Police Department investigated the case. Assistant U.S. Attorneys Mike Flesher and Jessica Wright prosecuted the case. Updated November 19, 2026 Component USAO - Oklahoma, Northern
